905.title: ig-ast-delta
905.content: Skill ig-ast-delta: List and view what changed between two IG ASTs, check whether an AST is still valid for the IG’s current inputs, and render the delta as just-the-docs pages that carry the provisional mark. Read before trusting a cached AST, before reviewing an incremental IG build, and before rendering anything from a cache. Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, Is the incremental IG AST what a full build would have produced?, SMART Guideline end to end . Skill id: ig-ast-delta · Package: fhir-ig-base · Layer: fhir-harness . An instance of the general compiled-artefact-cache pattern; the shared contract is cat-harness’s compiled-artefact-cache skill. The AST’s cache is declared once, as the cache/1.0.0 node caches/fhir-ast.cache.json: its verify is validity below, and its staleness is computed by caches:viz (see ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”). An IG AST is a per-resource dump of what one IG Publisher build held in memory. It is written by the ast-export library, which is built on top of the Publisher rather than inside it (litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher@claude/ast-export, ast-export/). This skill is the consumer half: listing an AST, checking it, diffing two of them, and rendering the result for a reviewer.

906.title: The one rule: a cache, never an authority
906.content: Every AST manifest says "authority": "cache" and lists what is provisional until a full Publisher run: indices, dependency edges and versions. Anything rendered from an AST, or from a delta between two, shows that mark to the reader, on the page itself (ig-publisher-reduction P3). A mark that exists only in a log or a JSON field does not count.

907.title: Where the files come from
907.content: | file | written by | says | . | manifest.json (ig-ast/v1) | AstExportCli, AstMerger | every resource with its key, the toolchain, the inputs the AST is valid for, and, on an incremental AST, mixed: true and builtAt per resource | . | dependencies.json (ig-ast-dependencies/v1) | same | every edge, resolved to a resource in this IG or null when the target is elsewhere | . | fsh-index.json | SUSHI (copied by AstExportCli) | the authoritative mapping from source .fsh file to output resource filename, with source line ranges. SUSHI writes it to fsh-generated/data/fsh-index.json; the copy lets a later delta map a file that has since been deleted | . | plan.json (ig-ast-plan/v1) | AstPlanCli | what a delta of changed files means: rebuild, load from cache, remove, or a full build and why | . | delta.json (ig-ast-delta/v1) | ig-ast.ts diff (here) | what changed between two ASTs | . The formats are declared once, and published as JSON Schema . The three ig-ast* formats are declared in Zod in fhir-harness/schemas/ig-ast.ts, and readAst validates through it. The JSON Schemas (draft-07) and a JSON-LD context are generated from that declaration and committed beside it: . | ig-ast.schema.json | ig-ast-dependencies.schema.json | ig-ast-plan.schema.json | ig-ast.context.jsonld | . bun run cat ig-ast:schema regenerates them and ig-ast:schema:check is the CI gate. The Java writer and any downstream consumer validate against these files. Every object is open to fields the writer adds first; authority is the literal "cache", and a manifest claiming anything else is refused. A resource’s key is canonical|version, or Type/id when it has no canonical. Two ASTs are compared by key. An incomplete AST is refused: a missing dependencies.json or a missing or unparsable resource file stops the command, because an empty substitute would diff as “no change”.

908.title: Commands
908.content: All of them live in fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts, and each is declared as a Tool: . bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts list <ast> bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts validity <ast> --ig <root> [--toolchain "<ig-publisher X / core Y>"] [--at <rev>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts digest --ig <root> [--at <rev>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts diff <base-ast> <head-ast> [--plan plan.json] [--json delta.json] [--site <dir>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts render <delta.json> --site <dir> bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts jsonld <ast> > ast.jsonld . validity: is this AST still the IG I have? . It reuses folio-assistant-core’s compiledValidity, the staleness check the Lean .olean cache uses. The Java side writes inputs in exactly CompiledInputsSchema’s shape: toolchain, sourceRevision, and inputDigest as 64 hex characters. validity recomputes the digest and the revision from the checkout and compares. | valid (exit 0): built from these inputs. | stale-inputs (exit 1): names which input differs. A changed input/ file is inputDigest; a newer Publisher is toolchain. | cannot-tell (exit 2): never a pass. A manifest without usable inputs, or with a digest in the older sha256:<hex> form, lands here. | . The digest is computed in two languages, Java when writing and TypeScript when checking. A golden vector (58871352384745e1d7fd68f7ea918b0e2febbd86cf36a9cb5f0c7ce9d13a82f1) is asserted by both test suites. If you change the algorithm, change it and the vector in both places; a drift makes every AST read as stale, or a stale one read as valid. A later commit that changes no input is the same source. If the recorded sourceRevision is an ancestor of HEAD and the recomputed inputDigest equals the recorded one, the revision counts as unchanged (sameSourceAs), so a README merge does not make the cache stale. A recorded commit the checkout cannot see (a shallow clone, another branch) stays stale. After a build, check the commit, not the work tree: --at <rev>. The Publisher writes under input/ during a build: it renders input/images-source/*.plantuml into input/images/*.svg, overwriting tracked files and adding untracked ones, so a work-tree digest taken after the build is not the commit’s and a freshly built AST fails its own check. validity --at HEAD (and digest --at HEAD) hashes the inputs as committed (inputDigestAt); in a clean checkout this equals the work-tree digest and the exporter’s. ig-ast-refresh.yml instead restores input/ with git before its check. The toolchain cannot be read from a checkout. Without --toolchain it is assumed unchanged, and the result’s current says so. When the Publisher you would run is known, pass it. diff: list what changed . Resources are added, removed, changed or versionChanged. A version move (same canonical, different version) is paired, not reported as a removal plus an addition. Each changed resource carries a differential: JSON paths whose value was added, removed or changed, capped at 200 rows per resource, with the overflow counted rather than dropped. Edges are listed as added or removed. --plan folds the incremental plan’s decision in. The differential is structural, over the dumped JSON, not FHIR-semantic: reordering a repeating element shows as a change at every index, and a narrative regenerated with a new timestamp shows as a change. Read it as “these bytes moved”, and judge meaning yourself. render: view it in the pipeline . --site <dir> writes just-the-docs pages: index.md (the list, grouped by resource type, with counts, the plan, and edge changes) and one page per changed or version-changed resource (path, op, base, head). | Every page opens with the provisional mark. Do not remove it to make a page look finished. | Liquid in values is neutralised, not merely wrapped. FHIR narratives carry Liquid output and tag delimiters (double braces, brace-percent). A raw block around the page is not enough: a value containing the raw block’s own closing tag would end it. So every value gets a word joiner (U+2060) inside each opening and closing delimiter; the text reads the same, and Jekyll parses nothing. This skill names those delimiters in words because its own reference page is rendered inside a raw block by gen-skill-docs; do not write the closing tag literally here. | One page per key, not per Type/id. Page names carry a hash of the key, as the AST’s own files do, so two versions of one resource are two pages. | Table cells escape |, which a key contains (canonical|version). | . Put the pages under the IG’s own just-the-docs site (see ig-render-jekyll) as a child section, so the reviewer keeps the site’s navigation.

909.title: Where this sits in a process
909.content: The review is drawn as its own subprocess, fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn. In fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn it belongs between Task_Merge (restored and rebuilt records merged) and Task_Qa (QC gates on the aggregate), which that diagram does not yet show: it is what the QC reviewer reads to decide whether the incremental result is what a full build would have produced. The steps, in order: . | validity on the base AST. stale-inputs or cannot-tell means no incremental build; run a full one. | AstPlanCli for the delta of changed files. The planner uses two maps: . | Forward (fsh-index.json, from SUSHI): which .fsh file produces which FHIR resource. This is the authoritative answer. | Reverse (fsh-file-users/v1, from fsh-cone --file-users): which files depend on a given file. This is how a changed RuleSet- or Alias-only file (which produces no resource itself) reaches the resources it affects. | . | IncrementalBuildCli (or a full build, if the plan says so). | diff base head --plan plan.json --site <site>/ast-delta/. | The reviewer reads the rendered delta. A difference they cannot explain is a missed coupling in the cone rules, not a curiosity: file it as a work item and run a full build. | .

910.title: Which rendered pages a source change reaches
910.content: Before any build, fhir-harness/scripts/ig-rendered-impact.ts predicts the rendered files a change to .fsh, .cql or input/pagecontent alters, through fsh-cone and SUSHI’s fsh-index.json, as a rendered-impact/v1 (skill rendered-impact in cat-harness). An AST diff afterwards confirms it: a resource the delta reports changed whose page the prediction did not name is a cone defect. bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-rendered-impact.ts --ig <root> --base origin/main --head HEAD [--ast <output-ast>] --out impact.json .

911.title: Do not
911.content: . | Do not treat a clean validity as a correct AST. It says the AST was built from these inputs, not that the build was right. | Do not diff a merged (mixed: true) AST against a full build and call every difference a bug. Check builtAt first. A resource carried from the base was not rebuilt, and the difference may be the change itself. | Do not render from an AST whose validity you did not check. | Do not re-implement any of this in a CI workflow. CI calls these same scripts and tools, so a CI result and a local result are the same measurement.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml (ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”) does exactly that: ig-cache.sh, ig-ast.ts validity and AstExportCli. | .

913.title: ig-build-pipeline
913.content: Skill ig-build-pipeline: The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository’s index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, Each IG, composed into a host docs site and rendered with just-the-docs . Skill id: ig-build-pipeline · Package: fhir-ig-base · Layer: fhir-harness . The base: run the FHIR IG Publisher over an IG, with no pre-processing and no post-processing, and publish the result. It serves any FHIR IG; see §”What this layer refuses to know about”.

914.title: The pipeline
914.content: input/fsh/ → SUSHI → fsh-generated/resources/ input/pagecontent/ ┐ sushi-config.yaml ┘ → IG Publisher (JVM, Docker) → output/ → publish to a pages branch . The publish target (the pages branch) is declared by the layer. SUSHI and the Publisher both need packages.fhir.org. Where it is refused, see fhir-validation §”When a package host refuses you” before concluding either cannot run.

915.title: Source of truth versus compiled, cached and rendered output
915.content: The boundary is declared in schemas/ig-content-type.ts: contentTypes.ig.include in index.config.json defaults to ["input/**", "sushi-config.yaml", "ig.ini", "publication-request.json"] and excludes output/**, temp/**, template/**, fsh-generated/** and input-cache/**. Only the files inside contentTypes.ig.include (plus any declared ig-annex directory) are hand-authored source. | Authoritative source (edit here) | Compiled, cached or rendered output (never hand-edit; overwritten on build or publish) | Basis | . | sushi-config.yaml (id, canonical, version, status, releaseLabel, fhirVersion, dependencies, pages, menu), ig.ini, publication-request.json | fsh-generated/resources/ImplementationGuide-*.json, output/, fhir-artifact-index/ig-identity.json, fhir-artifact-index/menu.json, fhir-artifact-index/releases.json, site.data.fhir | schemas/ig-content-type.ts (IG_DEFAULT_INCLUDE), ig-render-jekyll | . | input/fsh/**/*.fsh | fsh-generated/resources/*.json, fsh-generated/data/fsh-index.json, fsh-generated/includes/fsh-link-references.md (even when fsh-generated/ is committed in a legacy checkout, it is SUSHI’s compiler output — edit the .fsh source, never the generated JSON) | schemas/ig-content-type.ts (IG_DEFAULT_EXCLUDE), ig-ast-delta §”fsh-index.json” | . | input/cql/**/*.cql and input/maps/**/*.fml | Compiled Library (base64 ELM/CQL content[]) and StructureMap resources in output/ and output-ast/ | l3-fhir-authoring, ig-ast-delta | . | input/pagecontent/**/*.md, input/includes/**, input/translations/**/*.po, and declared ig-annex directories (annexes.json) | Rendered HTML in output/, composed thin pages in $SITE_WORK/ / docs/, and copied assets/annex/* | ig-render-jekyll §”Thin pages, the default”; §”The IG repository’s site route” below | . | input/images-source/*.plantuml | input/images/*.svg written by the Publisher when a same-stem .plantuml exists in input/images-source/ (hand-placed static assets under input/images/ with no .plantuml stem are source) | ig-ast-delta §”validity” | . | input/** + sushi-config.yaml + ig.ini | output-ast/ and the AST cache branch cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> (manifest.json with "authority": "cache", dependencies.json, fsh-index.json, expansions.json, txcache/), written only by ig-ast-refresh.yml | §”The AST cache lifecycle”, ig-ast-delta | . | The AST + sushi-config.yaml | fhir-artifact-index/ (index.json, menu.json, ig-identity.json, releases.json, sidecars/), <Type>-<id>.json, artifact/<Type>-<id>.{html,jsonld,json}, assets/ig-search.json, folio-build.json, and the published site on gh-pages (root and branches/<branch>/) | §”The IG repository’s site route” | . An overlay using pre-export or ig-site:sidecars documents its own authority table in its own skill. This layer puts back everything pre-export touched before it records the clean commit’s input digest (§”The AST cache lifecycle”).

916.title: Version numbering: SEMVER for a FHIR IG
916.content: An IG’s version is declared in sushi-config.yaml version (and mirrored in publication-request.json version when cutting a release). It is always an exact MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semantic version triple (versionIncrement: "major" | "minor" | "patch" in ig-publication; directory-conventions §”Pinning a reference”), never a range or floating tag. Which segment bumps is determined by the delta on the IG’s published conformance and canonical surface since the previous release — measured over the AST with ig-ast.ts diff <prev-ast> <next-ast> (ig-ast-delta §”Diffing two ASTs”), not from commit messages: . | Increment | What triggers the bump on a FHIR IG | Examples | . | major (X+1.0.0) | Any breaking change to the IG’s canonical conformance surface, terminology bindings, CQL/operation signatures or FHIR version that can invalidate a conforming instance or downstream dependent IG | Removing or renaming a canonical resource (StructureDefinition, ValueSet, CodeSystem, Library, PlanDefinition, Measure, Questionnaire, OperationDefinition, ConceptMap, StructureMap); tightening cardinality (0..* → 1..*, 0..1 → 1..1) or adding a new required (min >= 1) element or error-severity invariant on an existing profile or logical model; strengthening a binding to required or replacing its bound ValueSet incompatibly; removing or changing the meaning of a concept in a published CodeSystem; incompatible change to a CQL library’s public expression names/types or an OperationDefinition’s parameters; changing fhirVersion; or a breaking major bump in dependencies: | . | minor (X.Y+1.0) | Any backward-compatible addition to the IG’s canonical resources, profiles, terminology, logic or narrative structure | Adding a new canonical resource (profile, logical model, extension, ValueSet, CodeSystem, ConceptMap, Library, PlanDefinition, Measure, Questionnaire, ActivityDefinition, ActorDefinition, Requirements); adding an optional (min = 0) element, optional slice or warning/guideline-severity invariant to a profile or logical model; adding concepts to a CodeSystem or widening a ValueSet expansion (extensible / preferred / example bindings); adding examples/instances or new narrative pages in sushi-config.yaml pages:; or a compatible minor update in dependencies: | . | patch (X.Y.Z+1) | Any backward-compatible fix that adds no canonical resource and breaks no conforming instance | Narrative prose, layout or typo fixes in input/pagecontent/**; description, title, comment or mapping metadata edits on existing elements; translation updates in input/translations/**; fixing invalid example instances; bug fixes in CQL expressions or FML maps that preserve declared inputs, outputs and clinical/functional intent; or rendering/theme fixes | . Release vs development cycle and dependency pinning: . | Cutting a release (vX.Y.Z): requires human release-authorization (ig-publication), a full AST build (ig-ast.ts build-kind output-ast --require-full), status: active and releaseLabel: release in sushi-config.yaml, a matching version: "X.Y.Z" entry in publication-request.json, and every entry under sushi-config.yaml dependencies: pinned to an exact MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release version — never current, dev, a branch name or a commit SHA (checked by bun run cat check:published-refs). | Between releases on the default branch: sushi-config.yaml carries status: draft and releaseLabel: ci-build (or ballot during a ballot cycle) with the next target MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version. Pre-release ballot or candidate cuts may append -ballot or -rc.N while keeping the target MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH core. | Overlay co-versioning: when an overlay pairs the IG with an upstream domain model in index.config.json contentTypes, the overlay’s own skill defines how the two version numbers relate. | .

918.title: What the site build emits: thin pages, by default
918.content: The Jekyll phase emits thin pages: each artefact page and the IG’s artifacts.html and toc.html are a few KB that load their content from JSON-LD nodes (artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld and artifact/index.jsonld). Each artefact’s tab views (definitions, mappings, JSON and examples) are thin pages beside it, drawn from the resource’s JSON. The IG’s narrative pages keep their prose, with every piece of chrome linked rather than inlined. Full pages: pass --full-pages to gen-ig-pages.ts and stage-ig-sites.ts. What each page holds, and the QA over the nodes, is ig-render-jekyll §”Thin pages, the default”.

919.title: The AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST
919.content: Process: ig-ast-cache.bpmn. The declared cache. The cache branch is the cache/1.0.0 node caches/fhir-ast.cache.json (cache-first CI, rule 6), and ig-ast-cache.bpmn is its component of the harness’s one optional cache process: Task_Restore and GW_Valid are the component’s verify, and Task_Seed is its save. The dispatched AST refresh (Task_Dispatch, Task_Export, on the Java runner) stays this cache’s own save path. The node carries the key recipe (ig-ast.ts digest), the producer, the consumers, the save policy and the uses. The stored key against the key today’s inputs imply, and so whether the cache is stale, is computed by cat-harness-tools’ caches:viz, never written here. Only a step that builds or renders an IG restores it (owner, 2026-11-05: “not all rendering/CI/merge processes need all caches. be optimal”). A test shard, a gate or a merge job never does. The node’s materializes (output-ast/, input-cache/txcache/) is how a plan decides that: a target needs this cache when what it reads touches those paths. Its needs is layers-ref, so the layers are restored first. Every restore, verify and refresh prints one line in cached-step’s format, **cached-step ig-ast: hit|warm|miss** (exact) — <why>. Key `.` (`ig-ast.ts cache-line`). `warm` means the refresh applied a delta over an older AST. The key is the input digest: it is derived from the content of the inputs, so a merge or rebase that leaves them alone keeps it. Terms: . | AST: the per-resource dump the IG Publisher AST exporter writes (output-ast/; formats in ig-ast-delta). | Cache branch: cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> on the IG’s own repository. Its tip holds the AST, the Publisher’s expansions.json and its txcache/; each seed is a child of the previous tip, so every commit a site was built from stays reachable for pages that read the AST by raw URL pinned to that commit (owner, 2026-11-10; fhir-harness#325). <package id> is sushi-config.yaml’s id. | Valid: ig-ast.ts validity says the AST was built from the inputs the commit being published has (Publisher version, sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini, input/). | . The rule. | The site is built from the cache-branch AST; the publish runs no Publisher and never uses the Publisher’s HTML. Its first step is ig-site:ast (ig-repo-site.ts ast): ig-cache.sh restore --ig-root ., then validity, as ig-cache.sh verify does. §”The IG repository’s site route” has the steps after it. | The publish refuses an AST that is not valid: stale-inputs, cannot-tell, or no cache at all. It does not fall back to a Publisher build or to the Publisher’s HTML. A preview (a STAGING, non-release build) accepts a stale or cannot-tell AST by default (owner, 2026-11-05: “preview/staging (non release) builds can be on stale cache”): publish it at once, never wait on a cache refresh for it. SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0 makes a preview refuse one too. The root still refuses; folio-build.json records the verdict the preview was built on. | A commit that changes no input does not make the AST stale. If the recorded commit is an ancestor of HEAD and the input digest is unchanged, the AST is still valid (sameSourceAs in ig-ast.ts), so a README or workflow merge needs no rebuild. A checkout that cannot see the recorded commit (a shallow clone) reads as stale. It never reads as valid. | Only a Publisher run refreshes the cache. Whenever the IG’s source changes, someone has to run it. The workflow below is the usual writer. When its run is queued and the root has to go out, build it where the checkout is (owner, 2026-11-05: “local/agentic build and push to gh-pages”): bash fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast-build.sh --ig-root . (the workflow’s build step as a script; it needs Java, Maven, Node, Ruby and the Publisher’s network; pass the same --template-repo the caller gives the workflow as template-repos, e.g. --template-repo who.template.root=WorldHealthOrganization/smart-ig-template for a WHO IG, whose #current template the build server does not list), then bash fhir-harness/scripts/ig-cache.sh seed --ig-root . --push on the default branch, then the publish. Do not wait on a queued runner for a publish an agent can do. | . Who writes the cache: one workflow, here.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml (workflow_call) is the only writer. The IG repository’s site-publish.yml (the template) calls it as its first job, ast, so a publish refreshes the cache before it builds: a no-op when the cache is valid for the commit. No IG repository carries a workflow of its own for it. A repository that wants the cache refreshed on every push to its IG sources may add the optional caller templates/ig-repo-site/ig-ast-refresh.yml. One run: . | mounts the layers the IG repository’s index.lock.json pins; | restores and judges the cache for ref (default main); | if the cache is not valid, or force is set, runs the caller’s pre-export command when it gives one, then builds the IG with AstExportCli (Tool ig-ast-export, pinned ast-export-ref); | puts back what pre-export changed in the inputs, and checks that the new AST is valid for its own commit; | seeds the cache with ig-cache.sh seed --push, only when the commit is on the default branch with the tip’s inputs. Otherwise the AST is uploaded as a run artefact, output-ast. | . A stale cache is rebuilt incrementally; a release is cut from a full build. Step 3 does not always run a full Publisher build: . | When the cache is stale, the run is not force, and the caller gives no pre-export, it runs IncrementalBuildCli over the restored cache. That rebuilds only the cone of what changed and merges it over the cache (skill ig-publisher-fork). Its own plan falls back to a full build when it cannot tell, and a failure, or a merged AST that is not valid, falls back to AstExportCli. | A cache that is missing or cannot-tell, a force run, and a caller with a pre-export always build in full. A pre-export changes the work tree, which the incremental build refuses. | The run’s kind output, and ig-ast.ts build-kind output-ast, say which kind of build it was: full, or incremental (the manifest is mixed, with an incremental lineage). | A release is cut from a full build only. Any step that cuts a release runs ig-ast.ts build-kind output-ast --require-full, which exits 1 on an incremental AST. To get a full AST, run the refresh with force. | The site says which kind of build it came from. folio-build.json carries ast.kind beside ast.verdict (ig-repo-site.ts, the publisher-pages step). | . A preview is built from its own branch’s AST. The template’s ast job passes ref: github.ref_name, and when that run rebuilt without seeding, the publish job downloads the run’s output-ast before ig-site:ast runs, which keeps an AST already in the checkout when it is valid for the commit. So a branch that changes the IG’s inputs gets a preview of its own content, and the shared cache stays the default branch’s. folio-build.json names the AST it used (ast.commit, ast.verdict) beside source. Seeding is refused below 90% of the incumbent’s resources or edges (the no-shrink gate in compiled-artefact-cache). The run builds no site, writes no gh-pages and dispatches nothing. The Tool node is ig-ast-refresh. An overlay’s preparation: pre-export. Some IGs prepare their inputs before the Publisher runs: an overlay registers pages in sushi-config.yaml or generates resources from other sources. The caller passes the command as the optional pre-export input, written in its own workflow file. This layer runs it with bash at the IG root and knows nothing about what it does: the overlay names its own steps. The run records the clean source digest (ig-ast.ts digest) before pre-export, restores the inputs after the export, checks the digest again, and writes it into the manifest’s inputs (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). The prepared tree’s digest and the command go under preExport, so the cache verifies on any clean checkout. A failing pre-export fails the run, and nothing is seeded. When it runs. Only when a person, or an agent named for that run, dispatches it. An agent never dispatches it on its own (feature-staging §”Agent-run repositories”). Adding a push trigger on the default branch, filtered to sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and input/**, is decided per repository by its owner.

920.title: What this layer reads: contentTypes.ig.include
920.content: An IG repository declares which paths this layer reads in its root index.config.json; nothing else is read: . "contentTypes": { "ig": { "include": ["sushi-config.yaml", "ig.ini", "input/fsh/", "input/pagecontent/"] } } . The section is the ig content type (schemas/ig-content-type.ts). An entry ending in / is a directory and covers everything under it; any other entry is one file. Paths are repository-relative and POSIX: absolute paths, .., ., backslashes and empty segments are refused. sushi-config.yaml is not the marker: a repository is an IG source because it declares the section. Every IG reader here honours it. Each one asks scripts/ig-read-scope.ts (igReadScope(root)) before it touches a path: build-ig-indexes, ig-repo-site, build-ig-site, fsh-cone, ingest-ig-menu, ingest-ig-chrome, ig-api-hub, ig-site-data, ig-review-data, measure-logic-layer-edges and check-translation-supplements. An undeclared optional directory (input/images/, say) reads as absent; an undeclared file a reader cannot work without (sushi-config.yaml) is refused with the path named. ig-repo-site compose and stageIgSite stage from a copy of the declared paths only. Not gated: index.config.json itself, and the ig-ast.ts input digest, which must match the Java exporter’s. The list bounds the harness, not SUSHI or the Publisher. A repository that declares no section is a legacy IG. Every path is read, and each run prints one warning per repository: . warning: <root> declares no contentTypes.ig in its index.config.json, so fhir-harness reads it as a legacy IG (every path). Declare "contentTypes": { "ig": { "include": [...] } } there, listing the paths the harness reads (see fhir-harness schemas/ig-content-type.ts). When you see it, declare the section; do not silence the warning. A section that is there but has no include, an empty one, or a bad entry is refused outright: a section that declares nothing is never read as “everything”. Adding a path. When a page, a diagram or a data file is missing from the site and the IG declares the section, check include before the reader. Add the path to contentTypes.ig.include in the IG’s own index.config.json (a directory with a trailing /), in the same pull request as the content that needs it, and say in the description which reader needed it. Add the narrowest path that covers it, never "" or the repository root. Example: the WHO SMART Base IG includes input/diagrams/, input/archimate/, input/dmn/ and input/ignoreWarnings.txt.

921.title: The IG repository’s site route: the layers supply the steps
921.content: An IG repository declares no site.build. It holds index.config.json with "site": {"landing": "<layer>"}, and the site route (stage-local.ts, cat-harness-tools) asks the mounted layers’ script table for these step names, never naming a layer: . | slot | when | provided by | what | . | ig-site:ast | pre, required | this layer | restore the AST from the cache branch and judge it (rule 1 and 2) | . | ig-site:sidecars | pre, optional | the landing layer | the IG API sidecars from the AST, into $SITE_WORK/ig-api/ | . | render:bpmn | pre, optional | cat-harness-tools | the site’s drawing of every diagram, at docs/assets/img/workflows/ of the harness’s docs, which the process pages embed; built at publish, never committed | . | ig-site:compose | source, required | this layer | the artefact index from the AST, the thin pages, the IG composed at the root | . | ig-site:openapi | site, when the IG holds openapi/cat-openapi.config.json | cat-harness-tools | a page and an IRI for each OpenAPI operation, at openapi/ | . | ig-site:publisher-pages | site, required | this layer | the AST’s data served, the Publisher-chrome guard, the build stamp | . | ig-site:bar | final | this layer | the language picker and the IG’s slim bar on the pages the platform wrote after publisher-pages (ig-repo-site.ts bar) | . The handshake with a layer above (ig-repo-site.ts): . | Input: a sidecar step leaves its files in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/sidecars/. | Descriptor: what the IG calls them, in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/ig-api.json ({ "label": "..." }). | Binding: this layer binds whatever is there to the artefacts by the Publisher’s file names (ast-to-artifact-index.ts --sidecars), labels the pages with the descriptor’s label, and serves the files at fhir-artifact-index/sidecars/. It knows no producer and writes no label down; with nothing there it binds nothing and the pages say “IG API”. | Serving path: files the layer above leaves in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/site/ (its own pages over the sidecars, such as an OpenAPI page at openapi/index.html) are served verbatim at the site root, never over a path the site already holds. The Publisher-chrome guard judges them like every other page. | Placeholder exception: a page of the IG’s own that holds the descriptor’s "placeholder" marker is a shell around the layer’s content, and the layer’s page at the same path replaces it. No other page is replaced. | . What the site serves from the AST: each resource once, under the Publisher’s name <Type>-<id>.json at the root (the thin pages’ data, gen-ig-pages --compiled-data ., and the narrative’s links; no ast-data/ mirror, owner 2026-11-08), the artefact index at fhir-artifact-index/index.json, and the AST as site.data for the IG’s own pages. The grouping of the IG’s committed fhir-artifact-index/index.json is kept when it holds one, since the AST stops before the Publisher assigns categories. Annexes an IG’s pages load on demand (a data dictionary, say, rather than the full workbook): . | What an annex directory is: the one directory an IG repository declares for this layer, because the data is the IG’s own and no AST holds it. It is of the generic ig-annex kind (typologies/ig-annex.json) and holds annexes.json (ig-annexes/v1: { page, file, columns? } per annex, file beside it). The files themselves sit in a directory nested inside, declared with the producing layer’s own kind; this layer names none of them. | Who reads it: compose and stage-ig-sites.ts, through annexesFor. Each copies every file to assets/annex/ and mounts ig-annex.js on the page. An index also reads a committed fhir-artifact-index/annexes.json if present (legacy location; do not use). | Link check: a .md annex is appended to its page as written, so its links address that page, not the directory holding the file. The kind says so (shownOnPublishedPages), which keeps them out of the harness’s source-tree link sweep, and bun run cat check:ig-annex-links (scripts/check-ig-annex-links.ts) judges them from the host page instead: each x.html must be a page the IG serves, and each #id an id that page (its annexes included) carries. | .

922.title: The deploy phase
922.content: Deploying to a pages branch belongs to this layer: the history page, the CI build banner, the release-link fix, deleting files over 100 MB, and a deploy that retries on a ref conflict. Commenting on a pull request that a deploy finished belongs to cat-harness.

923.title: Who starts a build
923.content: Before an adopted IG repository publishes on its own, two questions are put to its owner: whether automatic gh-pages builds become manual-only, and whether to install the just-the-docs site. They are in fhir-ig-create §”4. Who starts a build”.

924.title: What this layer refuses to know about
924.content: A list, because “generic” is a claim and a list is checkable. fhir-harness must contain no reference to: . | dak.config.json (dak.json as upstream still spells it), the DAK logical model, or any DAK component | smart.who.int canonicals, or any WHO publisher metadata | the DAK API’s NAMES and its PRODUCTION — the label “DAK API”, the dak-api.html hub page and its DAK_API_* markers, and the post-processing that writes the sidecars. Rendering the sidecars an IG publishes is generic and IS here, as the IG API (ig-api-views.ts). A WHO layer passes its names in as configuration (--sidecar-label, --api-hub-page, --api-hub-markers, --api-placeholder); nothing here writes them down. The per-artefact .schema.json, .displays.json and .openapi.json sidecars are that API, not DAK’s. | the DAK pre- and post-processing steps, in either direction | anything in the authoring-who-smart-guidelines package | . The WHO package may reference this layer; this layer may not reference the WHO package. A violation fails no build on its own: the layer simply stops being usable for a non-WHO IG. Gate: bun run cat check:fhir-harness-exclusions (in smart-base). A mention is not a dependency. Comments, markdown, and JSON _comment or description values are counted and never graded. Code (string literals included), other JSON values, and BPMN outside <documentation> are graded. The DAK step names are read from the WHO layer’s own pre/post-processing tables, so this list does not restate them. It is a ratchet: existing hits are in a committed baseline, each with a reason. A new hit fails, and so does a cleared one the baseline still allows, until --shrink lowers it. Never widen the baseline to admit a hit: move the WHO-specific part up, or have the WHO layer pass it in as a parameter (the IG page generator’s --sidecar-label is that shape already).

925.title: Translation supplements: compiled on every pull request
925.content: An IG’s translated FHIR terms are CodeSystem supplements, one FSH file per locale in input/fsh/translations/<locale>.fsh. The IG build compiles them, but it is often not run on a pull request, so an IG repository copies templates/ig-repo-site/translation-supplements.yml into .github/workflows/ unchanged. Its one job is . uses: litlfred/fhir-harness/.github/workflows/translation-supplements.yml@main . which runs scripts/check-translation-supplements.ts (Tool check-translation-supplements). It compiles the IG’s CodeSystem, Alias and RuleSet entities with every translation file in a throw-away FSHOnly SUSHI project, requires 0 SUSHI errors, and checks that each supplement supplements a CodeSystem of this IG, designates only that CodeSystem’s codes, has the file’s locale as its language (and no designation in another), and that no CodeSystem id is used twice. An IG with no input/fsh/translations/ passes as not applicable. It reads only sushi-config.yaml and input/fsh/ within the IG’s include. Nothing is resolved at run time. SUSHI is the version scripts/ig-toolchain.env pins (SUSHI_VERSION; no IG’s sushi-config.yaml names one), installed from scripts/sushi/package-lock.json with npm ci --ignore-scripts; the check refuses a lockfile or binary of another version, and a test fails when the lockfile and ig-toolchain.env disagree, so a SUSHI bump changes both in one pull request. The FHIR core package for the IG’s fhirVersion is pinned by sha512 in scripts/sushi/fhir-packages.lock.json and fetched from the npm mirror; a fhirVersion it does not list is refused. SUSHI runs with a package cache made for the run and no network, and the run fails if anything but the pinned core package appears in that cache.

926.title: Generic post-processing scripts
926.content: strip_library_binaries.py and strip_library_content.py strip base64 payloads and inline CQL/ELM out of Library resources. Nothing in either is DAK-shaped: any IG depending on hl7.fhir.uv.cql produces oversized Library resources. They live in scripts/library-strip/ (byte-identical copies, with upstream commit, licence and hashes recorded, and a test that runs them on a non-WHO IG’s output). Three more generic transforms live here: generate_logical_model_schemas.py (a JSON Schema per logical model), generate_valueset_schemas.py (a JSON Schema per ValueSet, plus the enumeration-response schemas) and generate_jsonld_vocabularies.py (JSON-LD from ValueSet expansions). The test for this layer: a step that reshapes what the Publisher already emitted belongs here. A step that adds a constraint, a profile or a WHO-specific name stays in the overlay. The per-artefact API sidecars and their hub are the FHIR IG API above; only their DAK label stays in the overlay. The Tools are declared in fhir-harness/tools/.

927.title: Upgrading to the overlay
927.content: An IG that wants the DAK surface does not change this pipeline; the WHO harness above it (the WHO SMART Base IG, whose DAK document kind carries the pre/post steps) supplies them as an overlay. The base takes no position on whether an overlay exists, and must not gain a flag for one — a do_dak input at this layer would be this layer knowing about DAKs.

928.title: Version floating is real here
928.content: publisher.jar is re-downloaded from the latest release on every WHO build, so two builds of an unchanged commit can differ. If this layer pins instead, say so in the layer’s declaration and make the pin visible in the QA record.

929.title: ig-build-pipeline (skill)
929.content: The skill ig-build-pipeline as its source file fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md writes it, rendered by gen-processes-viz.ts because it has no instruction page on this site — do not edit here. All processes .

930.doc: Each IG, composed into a host docs site and rendered with just-the-docs
930.title: Each IG, composed into a host docs site and rendered with just-the-docs
930.content: Process_IgDocsSiteCompose · advisory · 4 step(s) . How a host docs site builds every IG it mounts INSIDE itself, so each IG’s pages wear the host’s chrome (one sidebar, one search, one language selector) rather than being a site of their own. Subprocess of Tool stage-ig-sites; reached from docs-site-publish’s Call_InstanceSites (skill docs-generation). NO IG PUBLISHER RUNS. build-ig-site turns the IG’s source into Jekyll source, with the Publisher’s site.data.fhir filled from the IG’s AST and sushi-config.yaml, and the host’s ONE Jekyll build renders it with just-the-docs (skill ig-render-jekyll). Which IGs is DATA: each instance whose fhir-artifact-index/menu.json records a source.of (the IG repository) and source.ref (the commit). No workflow and no step here names an IG. feature-staging.yml runs the same steps for a pull request’s preview, with --changed-files, so only the IGs a change reaches are rebuilt. 935.title: Incremental IG build
935.content: Process_IgIncremental · advisory · 19 step(s) . An incremental build for a FHIR Implementation Guide: compile, validate and re-render only the dependency cone of a change, then gate on QA and deploy. One change (a PR push or a push to main) runs: restore the derived state, compute the change’s dependency cone, compile and validate only the cone against the warm validator, re-render the cone’s records, rebuild the meta-index, assemble the site, gate on QA, then deploy; on main or a release only, seed the cache from the green build. An unusable cache falls back to a full build; an environment error stops the run and logs why. Advisory, like the other content-type pipelines: the package that owns the content owns what adequate means. i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i

937.title: Lanes — who acts
937.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | fhir-modeller | Starts the run with a source change, and owns every failure branch before the process ends rather than just stopping: Gateway_Valid’s no, Gateway_QcPass’s no and Gateway_Restore’s environment error each write to the work plan here, in Task_LogFindings, Task_QcBeans and Task_LogEnvError, before EndEvent_Findings, EndEvent_FindingsQc or EndEvent_EnvError. A run that stops short always leaves a record of why. The work plan is a data store these tasks write to, not a lane of its own. | . | Incremental build (system) | build-pipeline | Owns everything that stays inside the cone: restore the cache, compute the cone, check it out, compile and re-render only that slice, then merge and rebuild the aggregates — Task_Index never re-derives an artefact on its own, so a missing record is a miss rather than a silent rebuild. What needs the JVM’s warm state, it hands to Lane_Services rather than running itself. | . | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publisher-service | Two duties. Task_FullBuild is the fallback when Gateway_Restore finds the cache unusable: it bypasses the cone machinery and reaches Task_Qa on its own. Task_ContextLoad and Task_Validate hold the loaded dependency packages and expansions warm across runs, which makes validating a handful of cone files cheap; losing that warm state is a cache miss and routes to the fallback. | . | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | qc-reviewer | Sees the change’s shape before the build finishes — Task_ConeReport names what will rebuild and whether a shared hub is touched, posted while the checkout is still running — then gates on Task_Qa by reading the cone’s own rows in the aggregate first. On a PR branch it also deploys the preview itself, but never seeds the shared cache: that stays Lane_PubMgr’s, reached only past Gateway_Path on main or a release. | . | Publication manager — deploy and seed | publication-manager | Reached only past Gateway_Path’s main-or-release branch, never for a PR preview; the one lane allowed to touch the shared cache. Task_Seed writes to a -test branch and verifies a restore from a clean clone before promoting: the verified restore, not the deploy, licenses the shared cache. | .

938.title: Steps
938.content: Every one of the 19 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Restore derived stateTask_Restore | Incremental build (system) | ig-publication | ig-cache restore: the IG’s AST and the Publisher’s terminology cache (input-cache/txcache/). Exit 0 usable, 1 miss, 2 environment error, 3 present but unusable (corrupt or mismatched, such as a moved toolchain). The cache restored is the declared fhir-ast cache (caches/fhir-ast.cache.json), whose component process is ig-ast-cache.bpmn: this task is that component’s verify, run inside the incremental build. | . | Log the environment error on the beanTask_LogEnvError | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | todo-manager | Exit 2 from restore: the cache store or the toolchain could not be reached. Record that on the change’s bean, with the restore output, so the work plan says the build did not run and why. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. | . | Full publisher buildTask_FullBuild | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publication | Exit 1 or 3 from restore: the whole IG is built. Its outputs become the records the next seed writes. | . | Compute the cone of the changeTask_Cone | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | fsh-cone --changed (scripts/fsh-cone.ts) over the changed files: the forward cone is what to rebuild, the backward cone is what to check out. | . | Post the cone report on the PRTask_ConeReport | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | quality-controlquality-controlquality-control | Review path: the reviewer sees what this change rebuilds — how many artefacts, and whether a hub (a shared RuleSet, CQL library or value set) is touched — before the build finishes. On main it is a log line. | . | Restricted checkout of the backward coneTask_Checkout | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | git sparse-checkout of the cone’s files plus sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and the alias files — a median of three files, p90 eleven, measured on the SMART Immunizations IG. | . | SUSHI on the restricted tankTask_Sushi | Incremental build (system) | l3-fhir-authoring | Compile the restricted checkout with SUSHI — the cone’s FSH, not the whole IG. A build optimisation, not a validation shortcut: SUSHI compiling is not conformance, so a green compile goes on to validation rather than standing in for it. | . | Load or reuse the warm contextTask_ContextLoad | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | The validator’s server mode holds the loaded dependency packages, snapshots and expansions in its session cache. Cold start loads the restored derived FHIR rather than regenerating it. | . | Validate the cone (fhir_validate)Task_Validate | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | fhir-validation | Validate the cone’s resources against the warm validator and report the cone that was checked. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine, never a pass with no findings. A green cone is not a green IG: a profile the change did not touch can still be broken by it. | . | Log findings on the beanTask_LogFindings | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | todo-manager | Validation failed: record the findings on the change’s bean, so the work plan says what blocks it. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. | . | Re-render the cone’s records (fhir_narrative · skip lists)Task_Render | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | Narrative and fragments for the cone only: the publisher’s -no-validate / -no-narrative complements today, Rapido’s differential build once its tracker is persisted. | . | Merge restored and rebuilt recordsTask_Merge | Incremental build (system) | ig-publication | Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone’s freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact’s record and never re-derives one. | . | Rebuild the meta-index (ig_metaindex_rebuild)Task_Index | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | The whole-IG aggregates only — artifacts, TOC, canonicals, expansions, package, QA aggregate. Never re-derives an artefact: a missing record is a miss (exit 1), not a silent rebuild. | . | Assemble the siteTask_Site | Incremental build (system) | ig-publication | Assemble the site from the merged records: the IG template and a Jekyll build over output/. Only site assembly happens here — every artefact record already exists. | . | Run QC gates on the aggregate QATask_Qa | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | quality-control | qa.json is the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes; the reviewer reads the cone’s rows first. | . | File QC findings as beansTask_QcBeans | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | todo-manager | QC failed on the aggregate: file each finding as a bean, so it is tracked on the work plan rather than lost in qa.json. Check for an existing bean before creating one. | . | Deploy the preview siteTask_DeployPreview | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | content-publish | A preview never seeds the shared cache. | . | Deploy the siteTask_Deploy | Publication manager — deploy and seed | content-publishig-publication | Deploy the site built from main or a release. Deploying is release-management, after a human authorised the release — an agent never records that authorisation. Report the published URL only once it answers: a returned deploy is not a serving site. | . | Seed the cache from the green buildTask_Seed | Publication manager — deploy and seed | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | Only a green build of main or a release seeds. Seed writes to the -test branch, verifies a restore from a clean clone, then promotes. This is the save of the declared fhir-ast cache (caches/fhir-ast.cache.json), under its save policy: the default branch only. | .

939.title: Decisions
939.content: Every one of the 4 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Cache usable?Gateway_Restore | Answered by the exit code of ig-cache restore (Task_Restore): 0 is a usable cache and takes yes, into the cone machinery. 1 (a miss) or 3 (present but unusable) takes no, to the full publisher build, whose outputs become the records the next seed writes. Exit 2 (an environment error — the cache could not be read, which says nothing about whether it is usable) takes environment error: the run stops and the error is logged, so a broken cache store is not hidden behind a slow full build. | yes → Compute the cone of the changeno → Full publisher buildenvironment error → Log the environment error on the bean | . | Valid?Gateway_Valid | Answered by Task_Validate — the cone’s resources checked against the warm validator. yes goes on to re-render the cone’s records. no logs the findings on the change’s bean and returns them to the author. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine and does not take yes. | no → Log findings on the beanyes → Re-render the cone’s records (fhir_narrative · skip lists) | . | QC clean?Gateway_QcPass | Decided in the reviewer’s QC gate (Task_Qa, quality-control) over qa.json, the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes, reading the cone’s rows first. no files each QC finding as a bean, checking for an existing one first, and returns the findings to the author. yes goes on to deploy. | no → File QC findings as beansyes → PR branch, or main / release? | . | PR branch, or main / release?Gateway_Path | Answered by the push that started the process. PR branch is the review path: deploy the preview, which never seeds the shared cache. main / release is the publish path: deploy the site after a human has authorised the release, then seed the cache (Task_Seed). Only this branch reaches the lane allowed to touch the shared cache. | PR branch → Deploy the preview sitemain / release → Deploy the site | .

941.title: ig-publication
941.content: Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, Incremental IG build, L3 FHIR IG pipeline . Skill id: ig-publication · Package: fhir-ig-authoring · Named by activities in l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn (Build pipeline and Publication manager lanes) and ig-incremental-build.bpmn (Incremental build, Publisher + validator services (JVM) and Publication manager lanes). Build a FHIR Implementation Guide and publish it: version, tag, assemble the site, deploy. Sourcing. The IG Publisher and the FHIR publication process are HL7’s; an IG’s own publisher sets its release conventions. This skill states how publication is wired in this harness — which lanes, which authority, which binaries — and defers to those for what a published IG must contain.

942.title: Inputs and outputs
942.content: fhir-harness/schemas/skills/ig-publication/: . | in — igRoot (required), versionIncrement (required), releaseNotes, publicationTarget | out — version (required), publishedUrl (required), releaseTag, releaseBranch, publicationRequestPath, buildStatus | . How versionIncrement ("major" | "minor" | "patch") is chosen from the AST delta against the previous release, and which files in igRoot are authoritative source versus compiled, cached or rendered output, is defined in ig-build-pipeline §”Source of truth versus compiled, cached and rendered output” and §”Version numbering: SEMVER for a FHIR IG”.

943.title: Authorising a release is not the same as managing one
943.content: Two permissions, two holders: . | permission | held by | means | . | release-authorization | programme-manager, admin | may decide a release happens | . | release-management | publication-manager | may configure, build, version and deploy one that has been authorised | . draft-to-publication.bpmn marks Task_AuthorizeRelease and Task_PublishRelease relaxable="false": no package’s workflow-policy.json may relax either, with or without a reason. An agent never records the authorisation. skills/requirements/agent-workflow.json states it as a SHALL: an agent shall not record an approval, a sign-off or a decision to release on a human’s behalf. Building the artefact is this skill’s job; deciding it ships is not.

944.title: The toolchain
944.content: java -jar "${IG_PUBLISHER_JAR}" # default /opt/ig-publisher/publisher.jar jekyll build # site assembly . ig-publisher is a declared capability of this package and requires java-runtime; jekyll is not one of its declared capabilities.

945.title: What the Publisher run produces
945.content: The Publisher is one step in an IG’s build. An overlay may wrap it in pre- and post-processing of its own, which that overlay’s skills describe; this layer names none of them. The run itself produces: . | it produces | notes | . | output/ — the rendered site | HTML per resource and per page, from input/pagecontent/ and sushi-config.yaml’s pages: | . | {ResourceType}-{id}.json per resource | the structured surface everything downstream reads | . | .xml and .ttl per resource | not read, rendered or linked by this platform — see the JSON-only contract in ig-render-jekyll | . | package.tgz → package/.index.json | filename / resourceType / id, index-version 2 | . | canonicals.json, package.manifest.json | partial views of the same artefact set | . | artifacts.html | the only source of an artefact’s category | . | qa.json | the validation record, uploaded as a workflow artifact | . | POT files | extracted translatable strings | . It also does two things no post-processing step can. It validates every resource against its profiles and the declared FHIR version, and it resolves the dependency closure (hl7.terminology, hl7.fhir.uv.cql, hl7.fhir.uv.cpg, hl7.fhir.uv.crmi, hl7.fhir.uv.sdc for a clinical-reasoning IG) with version pinning and terminology expansion against tx. A cache cannot fake that resolution, which is why the phased transition keeps the Publisher for the AST and QA. Where it is invoked from . Inside Docker (hl7fhir/ig-publisher-base), with publisher.jar downloaded from the latest release on every run. The toolchain version is therefore not pinned: two builds of an unchanged commit can differ.

946.title: Full build versus restored state
946.content: ig-incremental-build.bpmn restores derived state and assembles the site without a full publisher run, fast enough for an authoring loop. A release is cut only from the full publisher build in that same diagram, in the JVM services lane. Never publish from restored state: the site looks right and was never built by the publisher the release claims produced it.

947.title: Report the URL only once it answers
947.content: publishedUrl is a measurement. A deploy that has returned is not a site that serves — GitHub Pages takes minutes on a first publish. Probe it, and until it answers report not-yet or unknown, never a live URL. scripts/pages-bootstrap.ts implements this three-state probe and decisions/pages-live-gate.dmn states the same logic as a table.

948.title: Pages of statements extracted from the IG’s sources
948.content: When the IG draws on library sources, the statements extracted from them are published as pages of the IG before the Publisher runs, each linked to its library entry and section. That is core’s standard step (publish-extracted-statements, bun run cat statements:pages), the same for every content type. What the IG supplies is its look, and nothing else: . | the page spec’s out is a page under the IG’s own page content directory, so the Publisher and the site route render it like any other page; | its tableAttr is the kramdown class the IG’s tables use (for example {:.grid}); | the page is registered in the IG’s own sushi-config.yaml pages and menu. | . statements:pages --check runs in the IG’s CI, so a page that no longer matches its extraction fails the build.

949.title: Afterwards
949.content: quality-control runs the QC gates on what was built; the summary goes on the issue, not only the PR.

951.title: ig-publisher-fork
951.content: Skill ig-publisher-fork: Requirements for an agent working a local experimental fork of the IG Publisher — which repositories, what the AST must carry, what must not change, and the acceptance criteria. Read before forking, and before reporting a fork’s work complete. Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch . Skill id: ig-publisher-fork · Package: fhir-ig-base · Layer: fhir-harness . The brief for an agent taking a local, experimental fork of the FHIR IG Publisher, so that an AST can be emitted and cached.

952.title: Which repositories, and why only one
952.content: | repository | holds | needed for | . | HL7/fhir-ig-publisher | orchestration, the loaded resources, DependencyAnalyser, CqlSubSystem, the metadata exports | the dump, the toolchain record, the logic-layer dependency edges | . | hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core | the renderer, the validator, dependency loading | page-fragment provenance only | . The logic-layer edges are a publisher-side gap, not a core one: . | DependencyAnalyser is in the publisher (org.hl7.fhir.publisher.core/.../igtools/publisher/). Its analysePD and analyseAD are empty stubs, and Library and Measure are not dispatched. That is the whole criterion-2 gap. | CqlSubSystem already attaches CQL depends-on to each Library (AdjunctFileLoader), so Library→Library edges exist in memory; nothing exports them. | . Only page-fragment provenance needs core. Read upstream before re-quoting either claim.

953.title: The shape taken: a library ON TOP, not a fork IN it
953.content: Do not change existing Publisher code unless there is no other way: remarshal, reuse, subclass. The work is ast-export/, a separate Maven project on branch claude/ast-export of litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher. It depends on the released org.hl7.fhir.publisher.core from Maven Central, is not a module of the root pom, and changes no Publisher file. | AstPublisher extends Publisher and overrides nothing. It reads getFileList() after execute(). | AstFieldsAccess is a read-only view of package-private PublisherFields, declared in the Publisher’s package inside the library. A rename upstream fails to compile rather than failing at run time. | Upstream’s DependencyAnalyser is reused unchanged; LogicEdges sits beside it. | . That makes “behind a flag, default byte-identical” true by construction for the Publisher itself: a stock build never loads the library. What still needs measuring is that AstExportCli’s own build writes the same output/ as a stock one.

954.title: The tools an agent runs
954.content: In the fork, under ast-export/: . | tool | what | network | . | scripts/run-real-igs.sh [work] [--byte-identical] | W1/W2 on the WHO SMART Trust IG and the WHO SMART Immunizations IG, W2 per resource type | packages.fhir.org, tx.fhir.org | . | scripts/w7-round.sh <work> | one incremental round on a one-CQL-file change | same | . | AstExportCli, AstPlanCli, IncrementalBuildCli | export, plan a delta, rebuild the cone | export and rebuild: yes; plan: no | . Here, ig-ast-delta lists, checks, diffs and renders what those produce. The one CI path is .github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml: it runs AstExportCli on a runner, at the pinned commit, to refresh an IG’s AST cache, calling the same exporter and ig-cache.sh. ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle” owns it. Any other CI calls these same scripts.

955.title: Without packages.fhir.org: seeding the cache from trusted sources
955.content: Some environments reach GitHub and registry.npmjs.org but not packages.fhir.org. The seeder fills the FHIR package cache from sources that are each a trust anchor: named by the owner, or the package’s own publisher. Nothing else is consulted. There are two copies: ast-export/scripts/seed-fhir-cache-from-npm.py in the fork, which ig-ast-refresh.yml runs, and scripts/fhir-cache-seed-npm.ts here, which the Tool fhir-cache-seed-npm invokes. | source | trust | what it holds | . | npm, account grahamegrieve | owner: trusted. Grahame Grieve founded HL7 FHIR | mostly the latest version of each HL7 package; core packages under @hl7/ | . | a publisher’s own published-site repository on GitHub | the publisher’s own published site | every released version that publisher hosts there | . | a template’s own repo at HEAD | FHIR/ig-registry/templates.json names it; owner: fhir.base.template is trusted | templates, #current included | . | --mirror | whoever ran mirror-fhir-packages.sh (Tool fhir-package-mirror) | what the others lack | . Rules: . | Exact versions only. A pin is never satisfied by another version; there is no “approximate” build with substituted versions. The one exception is the Publisher’s own rule: a patch wildcard (1.1.x) resolves to the highest 1.1.N a source lists, and the resolution is recorded. | Verified. npm tarballs against npm’s sha512. Every other source must carry a package/package.json naming exactly the requested package and version. npm’s 0.0.1-security malicious-package placeholder is refused. | Nothing computed once and kept. Load from the repositories every run; do not compute once and assume it fixed. The template registry, the IHE folder listing and any mirror clone are fetched fresh every run into a scratch directory deleted at exit. There is no table of package locations that could go stale behind the registry. | Provenance in ast-export-npm-provenance.json: the source, URL or commit, and hash of every package. | . Where it stands, measured over the WHO SMART Trust and Immunizations IGs: 20 packages install, including both templates. Missing are the pinned HL7 versions (IPS, terminology, extensions, CQL, CRMI, SDC, IPA), fhir.cqf.common and us.nlm.vsac. To close the gap: . | Run the seeder with --missing-out missing.txt. | Run mirror-fhir-packages.sh <repo> missing.txt on a machine that reaches packages.fhir.org. | Run the seeder again with --mirror <repo>. | . What the declared dependencies miss. Seeding from sushi-config.yaml alone leaves the build short (Publisher 3.0.0 / core 7.0.1): . | The template. It is named in ig.ini, not in sushi-config.yaml, so pass it to the seeder as a positional name#version. | A template seeded from its repo keeps the repo’s layout. The template’s own files go at the top of the cache entry, and only package.json goes under package/. The Publisher reads a cached template with NpmPackage.fromFolder, which files a top-level file under package/$root and unpacks it into template/. A file under package/ lands in template/package/, and the build fails with template/config.json not found. | Packages the Publisher loads by itself: . | hl7.fhir.pubpack at CommonPackages.VER_PUBPACK; | hl7.fhir.xver-extensions at CommonPackages.VER_XVER; | hl7.fhir.uv.tools.r<N> at Publisher.TOOLING_IG_CURRENT_RELEASE, for the IG’s FHIR release; | the latest milestone of hl7.terminology.r<N> and hl7.fhir.uv.extensions.r<N>, when the IG does not declare them. Read the versions from the release you build against. Never copy them from here, because they move with each release. | . | “Latest” offline is not exact. When it cannot reach the registry, getLatestVersion falls back to the highest version in the local cache. That silently breaks the exact-versions rule. Mirror the version the registry lists today, and record which version it was. | . An offline validator crash that is not ours. In core 7.0.1, InstanceValidator.checkTypeValue fetches the approved additional resources from fhir.github.io. When that fetch fails it dereferences a null set, so the build fails with an NPE on additionalResourceNames. Only an environment that cannot reach fhir.github.io meets it. It is upstream’s bug (org.hl7.fhir.core), and it is not patched here, because the library does not change Publisher code. Build with a terminology server. A -tx n/a build, which is run-real-igs.sh --no-tx, is only for finding faults before the real run. Its numbers are never recorded as measurements. A template the registry does not list is named by the caller with --template-repo <name>=<owner/repo>, on the command line, never stored. Publishers’ site repositories. The fork’s seeder keeps one fixed table mapping a package-name prefix to the publisher’s own GitHub repo. It can drift, which is tolerated only because every package fetched through it must name itself exactly in its own package.json, so a stale entry fails as “missing”, never as a wrong package. The copy here holds no such table: the caller maps each prefix with --site-repo <prefix>=<owner/repo>[@branch], none by default, because which publishers exist is not something fhir-harness may know. An IG’s package lock. An IG that pins its FHIR packages commits a fhir-packages.lock.json at its root, in the format of this layer’s scripts/sushi/fhir-packages.lock.json: {"packages": [{"name", "version", "tarball", "integrity"}]}, where tarball is an exact https URL (a commit-pinned one for a package a site repository publishes) and integrity is sha512-<base64> or sha256-<base64>; a hex sha256 may be given instead or as well, and every hash given must match. --lock <file> installs each pinned package from its URL only, refuses one whose bytes or package.json do not match, and does not follow its dependencies, so the lock lists the IG’s packages in full. ig-ast-refresh.yml (input package-lock, default fhir-packages.lock.json) and ig-ast-build.sh (--package-lock) run it before SUSHI and the Publisher, so neither fetches a package the lock pins. A package’s URL is named in the lock, never derived from its name.

956.title: The measurement that justifies the work
956.content: Using the Publisher’s current metadata exports as an AST proxy across two real IGs: . | export | the WHO SMART Trust IG | the WHO SMART Immunizations IG | . | valueset-ref-list.json ValueSet→CodeSystem edges | 17 over 14 | 431 over 252 | . | codesystem-ref-list.json uses populated | 0 of 15 | 0 of 14 | . | usage-stats.json extension→path | 6 | 35 (+5 profiles) | . Two findings: . | uses is declared and never populated — in both IGs. | Nothing exports Library / PlanDefinition / Measure dependencies — 458 artefacts, 61 % of the WHO SMART Immunizations IG, the decision-logic core, with zero edges. | . Re-derive both before quoting them. If a later Publisher release closes either, the fork’s scope shrinks accordingly.

957.title: Acceptance criteria
957.content: The AST must carry: . | one structured record per resource, keyed by canonical URL and version — an id alone collides across versions | dependency edges among Library, PlanDefinition and Measure — the gap above. Built as LogicEdges; not yet measured on the WHO SMART Immunizations IG. Measured as: every logic resource has at least one logic-to-logic edge in either direction. In graph terms, no vertex is isolated. Outgoing edges alone cannot be the test, because a finite acyclic dependency graph always has a sink: a library that others depend on and that depends on no logic itself. run-real-igs.sh prints both counts. | uses actually populated, or an explicit statement that it cannot be — a declared-and-empty field is worse than an absent one, because a consumer cannot tell “no dependencies” from “not computed” | page-fragment provenance — which source produced which output fragment, so a rendered page can be traced without re-running | the resolved dependency closure with pinned versions | terminology expansion provenance — which server, which version, and whether expansion actually happened; a build against a dead tx must be distinguishable from an IG with thin ValueSets | a toolchain object — publisher version, core version, SUSHI version. publisher.jar is re-downloaded from the latest release on every WHO build, so without this an AST cannot say what produced it | . And the fork itself must satisfy: . | emitted behind a flag, with default behaviour byte-identical when the flag is absent | upstreamable shape — a flag and an additional writer, not a rewrite; a fork that cannot be offered back has no exit | no change to validation or rendering semantics. If a fork build’s qa.json differs from an upstream build’s on the same input, that is a defect in the fork, and it is the first thing to check | .

958.title: What the agent must not do
958.content: . | Do not treat the AST as an authority. It is a cache: its indices, dependency edges and versions are unverified until a full run. Anything written to consume it says so — see ig-publisher-reduction §P3. | Do not vendor either repository into this one. The fork lives at its own remote; exactly one repository runs a thing. | Do not add WHO, DAK or SMART concepts to the fork. The AST is a property of a FHIR IG. A DAK-shaped field in it makes the fork unofferable upstream and breaks the layering fhir-harness exists to keep. | Do not fix uses by inferring it. If the information is not there, report that it is not there. An inferred edge in a dependency graph is indistinguishable from a real one downstream, and every ordering metric computed from it becomes unfalsifiable. | .

959.title: Reporting
959.content: A fork round reports: which repositories at which commits, which criteria are met, which are not, and what was measured rather than what was implemented. A criterion is met when an AST from a real IG is shown to carry the thing. The WHO SMART Immunizations IG is the right subject: it carries the 61 % gap.

961.title: IG publisher + validator — the role’s contract
961.content: Skill ig-publisher-service-contract: The contract the ig-publisher-service role is held to: what the JVM services an IG build shells out to must produce, and how a caller tells a pass from a run that never happened. A mechanical role’s skill is a contract to test against, not instructions to read. Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, Incremental IG build . ig-publisher-service in scenarios/roles.json is played by a mechanical actor (actorKinds: ["system"]; scenarios/actors/ig-publisher-service.json, which runs in the folio-assistant-smart-guidelines image). A role played by a machine is still a role, and its skills are its contract: the responsibilities it must perform, which a test can hold it to. Each line below cites the declaration it comes from.

962.title: What it must do
962.content: . | Build a FHIR Implementation Guide and report its QA — the actor’s description (“FHIR IG Publisher build and QA reporting”), and the qa-reporting action ODRL grants it in policies/ig-publisher-service.jsonld. | Complete the IG Publisher build with no errors in qa.html, after SUSHI has compiled the FSH — req:fhir-validation#ig-publisher-qa, which depends on #sushi-compile and which the ig-publisher capability (scenarios/capabilities/ig-publisher.json) declares it satisfies. | Validate individual resources and profiles against a package between builds — the fhir-validator capability, distinct from a whole-IG build. | Be detectable: each capability’s detection command answers --version / -version on a machine with a Java runtime (requires: ["java-runtime"]). | .

963.title: What it is not asked
963.content: . | To judge. The role is “external in behaviour, internal in configuration” (its description): it reports what the publisher found; whether a warning matters is the QC reviewer’s or the FHIR modeller’s call. | . No test in this repository runs the services — they run in a folio’s build, not here. The test in tested-by: holds lines 1–4 to what this repository declares: the actor and its ODRL grant, the two capabilities and their detection, and the requirement statement the publisher satisfies.
