4197.title: Signing and verifying an IRIS CDN release
4197.content: Skill iris-cdn-signing: How an IRIS CDN release is packaged, signed and verified using published standards only: a BagIt bag (RFC 8493), a detached JWS (RFC 7515 App. F) with ES256 (RFC 7518), and the key published in a did:web DID document whose publicKeyJwk carries an x5c chain up to WHO’s signing key. No GDHCN trust list is assumed. Named by: IRIS CDN initial load, IRIS CDN nightly change ingest, IRIS CDN weekly reconciliation, Sign and publish an IRIS CDN release . The code is scripts/iris-cdn/bag.ts and scripts/iris-cdn/signing.ts. The process is processes/iris-cdn-sign-publish.bpmn.

4198.title: Standards used, and nothing else
4198.content: | Piece | Standard | . | Package and digests | BagIt 1.0, RFC 8493: bagit.txt, bag-info.txt, manifest-sha256.txt, tagmanifest-sha256.txt | . | Signature | JWS compact serialization with a detached payload, RFC 7515 Appendix F | . | Algorithm | ES256, ECDSA on P-256 with SHA-256, RFC 7518 §3.4. It is the same curve as WHO’s signing DID key. EdDSA (RFC 8037) is accepted when verifying | . | Public key | JWK, RFC 7517, as publicKeyJwk | . | Trust chain | x5c in the JWK (RFC 7517 §4.7): X.509 certificates, leaf first, ending at one issued by WHO’s signing key | . | Key publication | W3C DID Core 1.0 document, verificationMethod of type JsonWebKey (W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0) or JsonWebKey2020, which is the form WHO’s own DID uses. Both are accepted | . | DID method | did:web | . No draft standards are used. A new one needs the owner’s explicit approval.

4199.title: What is signed
4199.content: There is one release signature, over the bytes of tagmanifest-sha256.txt, plus one signature per changed library item (below). The tag manifest pins the SHA-256 of every other tag file, and manifest-sha256.txt pins the SHA-256 of every payload file. Signing the tag manifest therefore covers the whole bag. The tag files live in the release git repository; the payload files live in R2 under sha256/<aa>/<digest>. The signature is stored beside the tag manifest as tagmanifest-sha256.txt.jws, in the form <header>..<signature>. The empty middle segment is the detached payload. The protected header is {"alg":"ES256","kid":"did:web:…#<key>"}. ECDSA signatures are randomized. Signing the same bytes twice gives two different signatures, so unchanged content is never re-signed: an unchanged night produces the same tag manifest and gets no new signature.

4200.title: A signature on each library item
4200.content: Every library item has its own manifest at items/<handle>/manifest-sha256.txt, in the same line format as the BagIt payload manifest. It lists the item’s record, records/<handle>.json, and every file under bitstreams/<handle>/. The item’s detached JWS is stored beside it as manifest-sha256.txt.jws. | An item verifies on its own. Fetch its manifest and JWS, verify the JWS against the DID document and its x5c chain, then check each digest. | The release signature proves completeness. The item manifests and their JWSs are payload files, so the release tag manifest pins them all. Nothing can be added or removed without breaking the release signature. | Only changed items are signed. If an item’s manifest bytes did not change, its existing JWS is kept (signItems in scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts). A metadata-only edit changes the record digest, so that item is re-signed while its PDF digest stays the same. | .

4201.title: Where the key comes from
4201.content: The verifier resolves the kid’s DID from the web, never from the package: . | did:web:<cdn-domain> resolves to https://<cdn-domain>/.well-known/did.json, and did:web:<cdn-domain>:iris resolves to https://<cdn-domain>/iris/did.json. The DID must be stable, because the DID is the signer’s identity. | When the DID document lists assertionMethod, the key must be in it. A retired key stays in verificationMethod so that old releases still verify, but it is removed from assertionMethod. A signature by that retired key on a new release then fails. | . If the DID document cannot be fetched, the verdict is unknown, not failed and not verified. A portal that cannot check says so. The trust chain. Our key’s publicKeyJwk.x5c holds the certificates that end at one issued by the key in WHO’s signing DID, did:web:raw.githubusercontent.com:WorldHealthOrganization:tng-participants-prod:main:WHO:signing:DID. The verifier is given WHO’s public key as its anchor, as the variable IRIS_CDN_TRUST_ANCHOR_JWK in CI. With an anchor, a key with no x5c fails. run.ts verify refuses without the anchor or IRIS_CDN_DID: the verdict is unknown and it exits non-zero. Called without anchors, verifyDetached reports the chain as not-checked, never as verified. No other trust anchor is assumed. A trust list, such as GDHCN via WHO SMART Trust, could only be an additional route to the same DID document, never a replacement for it.

4202.title: Key custody and rotation
4202.content: . | The private key is a JWK (kty: EC, crv: P-256, x, y, d). It never goes into git, a log or a bean. It is the GitHub environment secret IRIS_CDN_SIGNING_JWK in environment iris-cdn-release, which only jobs on main can read. | The key already exists. The subordinate key is already published in a DID document, with x5c up to WHO’s signing DID, before the exporter runs. That publication is offline and outside these processes. No CI job issues certificates or edits the DID document. | To rotate: . | Add the new key to the DID document and to assertionMethod. | Publish the DID document. | Sign the next release with the new key. | Take the old key out of assertionMethod, and keep it in verificationMethod. | . | The DID document is built in a fixed order, so republishing it with the same keys writes the same bytes. | .

4203.title: Verifying by hand
4203.content: In a checkout of the release git repository: . # 1. tag files against the tag manifest sha256sum -c tagmanifest-sha256.txt # 2. the release signature, with the key resolved from did:web IRIS_CDN_DID=did:web:<cdn-domain> IRIS_CDN_TRUST_ANCHOR_JWK='<WHO public JWK>' \ bun scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts verify --release <checkout> --no-revert . Payload digests in manifest-sha256.txt are checked against the objects at https://<cdn-domain>/sha256/<aa>/<digest>, not against files in the checkout.

4205.title: IRIS, DSpace and Dublin Core
4205.content: Skill iris-dspace: How WHO IRIS uses DSpace and qualified Dublin Core — the three identifier systems, MeSH as a controlled vocabulary, bundles, and the containment path — and the requirements a tool reading a record must meet. Named by: IRIS CDN initial load, IRIS CDN nightly change ingest, IRIS CDN weekly reconciliation . Every claim here is read off one captured record: the DSpace full item record for wpr-rdo-2020-003-eng, transcribed at catalogue/records/wpr-rdo-2020-003-eng.dc.json. Nothing is asserted from general knowledge of DSpace. Where this file and the record disagree, the record wins. The type is folio-assistant-core/schemas/dublin-core.ts. It is generic: Dublin Core is ISO 15836 and DSpace is a platform. This file covers only what IRIS does with them.

4206.title: Scale
4206.content: From IRIS’s storage report (By Location → Entire Site) and home page, read 2026-09-20: . |   |   | source | . | items | 273,559 | the home page’s search placeholder | . | files | 1,057,223 | the storage report | . | storage | 361.55 GB | the storage report | . | top-level communities | 8 | the storage report | . Items and files are different denominators, so catalogue/catalogue.json carries them in separate fields, totalItemsUpstream and totalFilesUpstream. That is 3.86 files per item, because an item carries several bitstreams. totalBytesUpstream is derived: the report prints two decimals and no byte count, so the value is round(361.55 × 1024³), good to about ±5 MiB. It is GiB rather than GB because every per-community figure the report prints (238.58, 19.72, 34.84, 26.14, 25.71) reproduces exactly at 2³⁰ and none does at 10⁹.

4207.title: Three identifier systems
4207.content: The worked item carries all three: . | system | value | authoritative? | . | DSpace UUID | 18892cf3-5a4f-42a4-923c-a93f4a594dec | no — IRIS’s own, stable only while this DSpace instance is | . | Handle | 10665/332098 | yes — guaranteed by the Handle System, outside WHO | . | WHO govdoc | WPR/RDO/2020/003 | no — WHO’s publication number | . The library slug wpr-rdo-2020-003-eng is derived from the govdoc, the weakest key. A tool that resolves by Handle survives the source moving. A legacy handle is live in the record, and must not be deduplicated . dc.identifier.uri appears twice: . https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/332098 ← global http://iris.wpro.who.int/handle/10665.1/14518 ← regional, merged away . Regional IRIS instances were folded into the global one and both URIs were kept. The second is a real alternate identifier, and evidence that a source host can disappear (the sourceLoss gate’s worked example).

4208.title: Qualified, repeated, language-tagged
4208.content: Every field is element.qualifier. Four fields repeat in this one record (dc.date.accessioned, dc.date.available, dc.identifier.uri, dc.subject.mesh), so Record<string, string> silently keeps the last value and drops the rest. There is a per-field language column, present on dc.title, dc.description and each dc.subject.mesh, absent on the author, the dates and the identifiers. An absent tag is not en: it is a value whose language nobody asserted.

4209.title: MeSH is a controlled vocabulary, not a keyword
4209.content: dc.subject.mesh = Publishing, Guidelines as Topic. These are NLM Medical Subject Headings, with their own identifiers and hierarchy at https://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/. A MeSH term can be resolved and subsumed (searching “Guidelines as Topic” should reach narrower terms); a free-text keyword can do neither. DcValue.authority records the distinction per value.

4210.title: An item is not a file: bundles
4210.content: DSpace groups bitstreams into bundles — conventionally ORIGINAL, plus TEXT (extracted), THUMBNAIL and LICENSE. Size and format are per-bitstream: the 2.68 MB in the record is the PDF’s, not the item’s. Bundles are why there are more files than items.

4211.title: Containment is a path, not a parent
4211.content: The breadcrumb: Home → 7. Regional Office for the … → Regional Office for the W… → Information products — four levels, two of them communities and one a collection. DSpace also lets an item be mapped into several collections, so “the” parent of a node does not exist. CatalogueNode.parents is a list of paths.

4212.title: What a later tool needs — as requirements
4212.content: | # | requirement | why, in one line | . | R1 | Resolve by Handle where one exists; treat UUID and govdoc as secondary | only the Handle is guaranteed outside WHO | . | R2 | Never deduplicate dc.identifier.uri | the second one is evidence of a host that vanished | . | R3 | Preserve repetition on every field, not a known list | four fields repeat in a single record; assume more do | . | R4 | Treat an absent language as unasserted, never as en | both states occur in one record | . | R5 | Carry dc.subject.mesh as a controlled value with its authority | it can be resolved and subsumed; a keyword cannot | . | R6 | Model bitstreams per bundle, with size and format on the bitstream | an item is not a file | . | R7 | Model containment as a list of paths | four levels deep, and multiple mappings are legal | . | R8 | Never infer metadata from the PDF when a record exists | OCR off a title page catalogued the WHO Editorial Style Manual as Abies | . | R9 | Record what the source says even when it contradicts the file | dc.description says 30 p.; the PDF has 33 | . | R10 | An item with no known collection carries parents: [] — never a guessed one | held-and-unplaceable is a STATE; inventing containment is unfalsifiable | . | R11 | Key a node by path when its UUID is not in the capture | an invented UUID resolves to nothing while looking authoritative | . | R12 | Keep the page captured and the identifier apart | /items/<uuid>/full is what was fetched; the Handle is what the item IS | . | R13 | A materialized claim must name bytes that EXIST, and something must check it | an unchecked claim can name no bytes and still pass as held | . | R14 | Read a storage figure in the units that round-trip its own bytes | IRIS prints “GB” for what its byte counts make GiB — a 7% error | . | R15 | Never fall back to a parent URL when an item has no upstream URI | “no upstream URI recorded” is the answer; the front page is a lie that resolves | . | R16 | A partial transcription must SAY it is partial | a truncated abstract that does not declare itself cannot be told from a short one | . | R17 | Hold what you hold: model the bitstreams whose bytes are here | the handbook lists 8 upstream; this repository has 1 | . | R18 | Do not “correct” a record that looks wrong | the English-titled editorial manual really does carry an Italian ISBN | . | R19 | A derived figure must round-trip the figure it was derived from | round(361.55 × 1024³) bytes must render back as 361.55 GiB | . | R20 | An item count and a file count are different denominators | 273,559 against 1,057,223 — a fraction built from the wrong one is off by 3.86× | . | R21 | Mint stable URIs at the extractor (Upstream Skolemization) | minting https://iris.who.int/entity/item/{handle}#{prop}_{idx} at extraction leaves no blank nodes for a later pass to resolve | . | R22 | Append-only streaming partition writes | A 300,000 item corpus cannot accumulate uncompressed in working memory; write quads directly to partition file streams | . R8: where a library entry’s title comes from . who-pub-tps-931 shows why. Its structure.json carries title: "Abies" and authors_raw: "Cpe N" — OCR noise off a scanned title page of the WHO Editorial Style Manual. 9789241548960-eng has three renderings of one title from the PDF (Handbook forGuideline Development 2nd edition from joined title lines, GRC Handbook - second edition from PDF docinfo, and the real one) and no authority among them. The IRIS record settles both. A library entry’s title is taken, in order, from: . | the catalogue record: dc.title of the Dublin Core record that the catalogue node naming the entry (libraryId) points at through metadataRef; | referenced.json identity.title; | the PDF Info /Title (structure.json metadata.docinfo.Title), only when it is not junk such as Microsoft Word - …, a file name, untitled, or an arXiv stamp; | the slug, which check:library-qa then reports as title-missing. | . The page-1 front-matter parse is never a title. It may still feed search and the section files’ doc_title. The manifest records which source won as meta.title_source (for example dc-record) and where it came from as meta.title_from, so R8 can be checked. The resolver is cat-harness-tools/pipeline/library-title.ts; the library-ingestion skill carries the full rule.

4213.title: Covers: an artefact we made, filed where IRIS files its own
4213.content: The replica’s home page shows a cover beside each item in its Recent Submissions strip, and each library entry page shows it too. None of them came from IRIS. Each is page 1 of the item’s PDF, rasterised by cat-harness-tools/scripts/pdf-cover.py and filed as a THUMBNAIL-bundle bitstream — the bundle name DSpace uses for the thumbnails it generates. Nothing downstream can tell the two apart from the bundle name, so the bitstream’s materialization.note must say the cover was derived here. The PDF is either held in this repository or, for a referenced item, fetched by the iris-cover-pdfs GitHub workflow, matched against the sha256 its ORIGINAL bitstream records, rendered and discarded. Only the cover PNG is committed. folio-assistant-core/scripts/gen-covers.ts (bun run iris:covers) renders only covers the catalogue asks for: a node declares the THUMBNAIL bitstream and the script supplies the bytes. It refuses to write bytes for a THUMBNAIL whose materialization.note does not declare the derivation, since a tool cannot attest to its own output. bun run iris:covers:check compares the bytes, the recorded sha256 and the recorded pixel dimensions, re-rendering where the PDF is held. That is R13 for covers. A cover whose PDF is not held can be verified but not re-rendered. The WHO emblem is masked on covers . The site chrome carries no WHO mark until the replica is published under WHO. Covers are shown with the WHO emblem and wordmark blanked to flat grey before the PNG is written, so the committed bytes never contain it. Each THUMBNAIL bitstream declares the blanked rectangles and the reason as maskedRegions. A title that contains “WHO” is not masked: it is the work’s name. A cover whose publication gates block it is shown as cover withheld, not no cover.

4214.title: Getting a record
4214.content: DSpace 7 exposes /server/api/discover/search/objects, paged and filterable by dsoType, scope and facets; communities are listed at /community-list. The calls this repository makes, and what live IRIS accepts, are in iris-rest-feed; the code is scripts/iris-cdn/rest-feed.ts. A record derived from a PDF rather than transcribed from IRIS must be marked derived, so it can be replaced wholesale when the real record arrives with nothing downstream having believed it. Enumeration cost, subsetting and the characterisation that decides whether IRIS may be cited at all are in who-iris/sources/who-iris.json.

4216.title: Oxigraph multi-graph search for WHO IRIS
4216.content: Skill iris-oxigraph: How to build WHO IRIS catalogue and Qualified Dublin Core metadata into partitioned N-Quads, and query it with Oxigraph — in Bun on the build side, in WebAssembly in the browser — including cross-graph joins and facet counts. Named by: IRIS CDN initial load, IRIS CDN nightly change ingest, IRIS CDN weekly reconciliation . The IRIS catalogue and its Dublin Core records are compiled into named graphs and queried with Oxigraph: natively in Bun at build time, and as WebAssembly in a browser. One SPARQL query can then join Dublin Core properties, catalogue containment and bitstream access gates — which DSpace Discovery cannot do in a single call.

4217.title: Build and query
4217.content: # Build from catalogue/nodes and site/dublin-core into dist/oxigraph/ bun run scripts/build-iris-oxigraph.ts # Build from exported DSpace records (the CDN release's records/ tree) bun run scripts/build-iris-oxigraph.ts --records <dir> --out <dir> # Load dist/oxigraph/who-iris-dataset.nq and run sample searches and facets bun run scripts/iris-oxigraph-search.ts bun test scripts/tests/iris-oxigraph.test.ts . scripts/iris-oxigraph-search.ts exports IrisOxigraphEngine (loadSpine, loadCommunity, searchSpine, complexSearch, facetCounts). The CDN exporter (scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts) calls the build over exported records and publishes each output file as graph/<file>.

4218.title: 1. Graphs and files
4218.content: The build writes, sorted and de-duplicated so unchanged inputs give byte-identical files: . | Tier 1, the spine — <https://iris.who.int/graph/spine>, in who-iris-spine.nq and .nq.gz. Hierarchy (dspace:Community, dspace:Collection), item Handles, titles, first creator, issued date, and bitstream descriptors with copyright verdicts. Loaded first. | Tier 2, one partition per community — <https://iris.who.int/graph/community/{id}>, in iris_who_int_graph_community_{id}.nq and .nq.gz. The full Dublin Core of that community’s items: MeSH authorities, abstracts, spatial coverage, govdoc numbers, ISBNs. Mounted on demand. | Catalogue and metadata graphs — <https://iris.who.int/graph/catalogue> and <https://iris.who.int/graph/metadata>, each in its own iris_who_int_graph_{catalogue,metadata}.nq(.gz), and merged in who-iris-dataset.nq and .nq.gz for server-side use and integrity checks. | subgraph-manifest.json — the spine and each community partition, with file names, quad counts and item counts. | queries.json — prepared SPARQL queries. | . Namespaces . | dspace: = https://iris.who.int/ns/dspace# — catalogue terms (Item, inCommunity, hasBitstream, fileName, …). | dspaceNs: = https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant-core/v0/ns/dspace/ — Dublin Core value terms, including authority. | . No binary bytes in the graph . PDFs, cover images and archives are never stored as literals. A bitstream node carries only: . | dspace:fileName (e.g. "WPR-RDO-2020-003-eng.pdf") | dspace:mediaType (e.g. "application/pdf") | dspace:fileBytes (integer) | dspace:copyrightGate — the copyright gate’s verdict, e.g. "permitted" | . The bytes are fetched from the CDN.

4219.title: 2. Requirements
4219.content: | # | Requirement | Why, in one line | . | OX-1 | Mint stable URIs at the extractor (https://iris.who.int/entity/item/{handle}#{prop}_{idx}); the build fails if any blank node remains | no multi-document collisions, every node addressable, no normalizer pass | . | OX-2 | Store zero binary bytes in RDF | keeps WASM memory small; binaries are static files on the CDN | . | OX-3 | Join across named graphs with explicit GRAPH blocks | separates containment and rights from bibliographic description | . | OX-4 | Use Handle URIs as the item subject (https://hdl.handle.net/...) | identity resolves outside WHO’s servers | . | OX-5 | Treat bitstream rights as access gates | results can be filtered by whether the PDF may be downloaded | . | OX-6 | Partition by community | a client fetches only the slice it needs | . | OX-7 | Never scan whole-corpus text in SPARQL | full text belongs in a static inverted index | . | OX-8 | Preserve controlled-vocabulary authorities (dspaceNs:authority) | distinguishes MeSH headings from free keywords | . | OX-9 | Append-only streaming partition emission | bounded memory at 300,000 items. Not met yet: buildIrisDataset holds and sorts every quad in memory; StreamingPartitionWriter is defined but unused | .

4220.title: 3. SPARQL recipes
4220.content: Recipe 1: multi-condition search . Items in the Western Pacific community, issued in or after 2000, with a subject containing “guidelines”, and a PDF whose copyright verdict is permitted. PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/> PREFIX dspace: <https://iris.who.int/ns/dspace#> PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> SELECT DISTINCT ?handle ?title ?creator ?issued ?pdfName WHERE { # 1. Join Dublin Core Metadata GRAPH <https://iris.who.int/graph/metadata> { ?handle dcterms:title ?title ; dcterms:creator ?crNode ; dcterms:subject ?sNode . ?crNode rdf:value ?creator . ?sNode rdf:value ?subject . OPTIONAL { ?handle dcterms:issued ?issued } } # 2. Join Catalogue Hierarchy & Access Gates GRAPH <https://iris.who.int/graph/catalogue> { ?handle dspace:inCommunity ?comm ; dspace:hasBitstream ?bs . ?comm rdfs:label ?commLabel . ?bs dspace:mediaType "application/pdf" ; dspace:fileName ?pdfName ; dspace:copyrightGate "permitted" . } # 3. Multi-Field Filter Evaluation BIND(IF(BOUND(?issued), xsd:integer(SUBSTR(STR(?issued), 1, 4)), 0) AS ?year) FILTER ( CONTAINS(LCASE(?subject), "guidelines") && CONTAINS(LCASE(?commLabel), "western pacific") && (?year >= 2000) ) } ORDER BY DESC(?year) . Recipe 2: facet counts . Item counts per subject term and its authority. PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/> PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> PREFIX dspaceNs: <https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant-core/v0/ns/dspace/> SELECT ?subject (COUNT(DISTINCT ?handle) AS ?itemCount) ?authority WHERE { GRAPH <https://iris.who.int/graph/metadata> { ?handle dcterms:subject ?sNode . ?sNode rdf:value ?subject . OPTIONAL { ?sNode dspaceNs:authority ?authority } } } GROUP BY ?subject ?authority ORDER BY DESC(?itemCount) ?subject .

4221.title: 4. Browser pattern: spine first, communities on demand
4221.content: import oxigraph from 'oxigraph'; // Where the graph files are served from, e.g. a release's graph/ directory. const BASE = '<graph-base-url>'; async function gunzipText(resp: Response): Promise<string> { const stream = resp.body!.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('gzip')); return new Response(stream).text(); } const store = new oxigraph.Store(); // 1. Fetch the spine and the manifest const [spineResp, manifestResp] = await Promise.all([ fetch(`${BASE}/who-iris-spine.nq.gz`), fetch(`${BASE}/subgraph-manifest.json`), ]); const manifest = await manifestResp.json(); // 2. Load the spine: hierarchy, title search and rights filtering work now store.load(await gunzipText(spineResp), { format: 'application/n-quads' }); // 3. Mount a community when the user selects it. load() adds its named // graph without clobbering what is already in the store. async function mountCommunity(commId: string) { const partition = manifest.tiers.tier2_communities.partitions[commId]; if (!partition) return; const resp = await fetch(`${BASE}/${partition.fileGz}`); store.load(await gunzipText(resp), { format: 'application/n-quads' }); } // 4. Run a prepared query locally for (const binding of store.query(myPreparedQuery)) { console.log(binding.get('title').value); } .

4223.title: Reading IRIS changes over DSpace REST
4223.content: Skill iris-rest-feed: How to read changes from the WHO IRIS DSpace 7 REST API: the nightly “changed since” walk over Discovery, the weekly reconciliation that stands in for the deletions REST does not report, and the guard that stops a short listing from reading as a mass withdrawal. Named by: IRIS CDN initial load, IRIS CDN nightly change ingest, IRIS CDN weekly reconciliation . Changes are read from the DSpace REST API only. REST has no change feed with deletions, so a nightly walk is paired with a weekly reconciliation. The code is scripts/iris-cdn/rest-feed.ts; its tests run on fixtures in scripts/tests/iris-cdn.test.ts.

4224.title: What live IRIS accepts
4224.content: . | Discovery offers only five sortOptions: score, dc.title, dc.date.issued, dc.date.accessioned, dc.date.available. sort=lastModified,DESC returns HTTP 422. | Changes are found with a Solr range query instead: query=lastModified:[<isoZ> TO *]. | The bound must be a Z-suffixed UTC timestamp. A +00:00 offset returns totalElements: 0. | .

4225.title: Endpoints
4225.content: | Use | Request | . | Changed items since cursor | GET /server/api/discover/search/objects?dsoType=ITEM&query=lastModified:[{isoZ} TO *]&sort=dc.date.accessioned,DESC&page=N&size=100 | . | Weekly full item listing | GET /server/api/discover/search/objects?dsoType=ITEM&sort=dc.date.accessioned,DESC&page=N&size=100 | . | Collection-scoped batch (initial load) | GET /server/api/discover/search/objects?dsoType=ITEM&scope={collectionUuid}&sort=dc.date.accessioned,DESC&page=N&size=100 | . | Communities / collections with parent | GET /server/api/core/{communities|collections}?page=N&size=100&embed=parentCommunity | . | One item with its files and collection | GET /server/api/core/items/{uuid}?embed=bundles/bitstreams&embed=owningCollection | . | Bundle bitstreams beyond page 0 | GET /server/api/core/bundles/{bundleUuid}/bitstreams?page=N&size=100 | . | A file’s bytes | GET /server/api/core/bitstreams/{uuid}/content | .

4226.title: Nightly: changedSince(cursor)
4226.content: . | Normalise cursor to UTC Z (new Date(Date.parse(cursor)).toISOString()) and run the range query above. | Page through the matching result set. | The cursor is inclusive: an item modified at that instant is read again, not missed. Re-reading an unchanged item writes the same bytes. | Return the items oldest first, de-duplicated by UUID. | . The cursor is the newest lastModified read, kept in state/cursor.json. A failed night does not advance it.

4227.title: Metadata changes without the PDF changing
4227.content: A PDF may stay the same while its Dublin Core changes. Records and files are handled separately: . | A record is re-read whenever its item appears in the walk. A PDF is re-fetched only if its DSpace MD5 changed. | Communities and collections are re-read in full every night (allContainers). A renamed collection changes no item, and DSpace 7 does not expose lastModified for these. An unchanged one serializes to the same bytes. | The weekly metadata check. The weekly listing pages carry each item’s metadata. metadataSha hashes it canonically, and any item whose hash differs from the one last ingested is re-read. That catches edits that did not move lastModified, without one fetch per item. | .

4228.title: Weekly: allItems and withdrawnOrHidden
4228.content: . | List every item ID Discovery returns. | Compare that list with the IDs the library holds. | Guard. If more than 1% of held items are missing, the listing is treated as faulty and nothing is marked. Possible causes are a paging fault, an outage or a Solr reindex. | Re-fetch each missing item by ID. Mark it withdrawn only if IRIS confirms it: withdrawn: true, or a 404 (gone), 401 or 403 (private). | .

4229.title: Fixity
4229.content: DSpace reports an MD5 checkSum for each bitstream. Downloaded bytes must match it before their SHA-256 is recorded. A mismatch quarantines the bitstream and reports it. It is never retried silently.

4230.title: Politeness
4230.content: Requests are made one at a time, with a User-Agent that names the project and its repository, and back off on 429 and 503. The initial load is paced to the budget stated in Task_StateBudget (processes/iris-cdn-initial-load.bpmn), including maxRequestsPerSecond.

4231.title: A subset by reference: run.ts subset
4231.content: bun scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts subset catalogues part of IRIS without fetching any bytes (who-iris#207): for each item, the Dublin Core record as DSpace returns it and a referenced catalogue node whose ORIGINAL bitstreams link to https://iris.who.int/bitstreams/{uuid}/download. The subsets it reads live in scripts/iris-cdn/subsets/. | Which items. A handles file goes first (for example the IRIS items a DAK cites), then a Discovery query. The query is a field query on metadata (dc.title, dc.subject, dc.subject.mesh, dc.description.abstract), not a bare keyword. A bare keyword also searches the PDF text, so vaccine matches a report that mentions one in passing. | Write boolean operators in capitals. Solr reads a lowercase or as a word: HIV or immunization or vaccine matches fewer items than vaccine alone. | A Handle to an item: GET /server/api/pid/find?id=hdl:{handle} answers 302 to /server/api/core/items/{uuid}. | An ISBN or govdoc to an item: query=dc.identifier.isbn:"{isbn13}" or query=dc.identifier.govdoc:"WHO/HIV/2017.09". | A sample is one-row pages at seeded random offsets, so the same seed gives the same items. | No fixity is claimed. IRIS reports an MD5. A sha256 is recorded only once the bytes are fetched (R13), so the MD5 goes in the bitstream’s note. | Hand-made nodes win. An item whose Handle or UUID another node already carries is skipped and reported. The tool rewrites only its own nodes, the ones whose note starts “Catalogued by reference by scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts subset”, and only when they changed. | A token, when IRIS gives one, comes from the IRIS_DSPACE_TOKEN environment variable as Authorization: Bearer …. It never appears in an argument, a file or a log. | .

4233.title: Knowledge graph affordances — browse, materialise, instantiate, copy-into-folio
4233.content: Skill kg-affordances: The four affordances of a conformant knowledge graph — browse, materialise, instantiate and copy-into-folio — which capabilities each requires, how each writing verb degrades cleanly when no write capability is available, and how copying an asset stamps KgAsset.source provenance. Named by: Content acquisition, Copy out materialized content — to work on somebody else’s bytes, Basic ingestion — an upload to an asset catalogued in library/, Materialize remote content: the shared subprocess, Adopt a methodology from a source document, Multi-locale translation, Refresh materialized remote content, Sample import into a structured data store, Subscribe to an external knowledge graph, Translation Workflow, Review task, Copy a knowledge-graph asset into a folio, A sub-graph wants to leave, Authorise the extraction, Move the graph into its repositories, Prepare a graph to stand alone, A knowledge graph leaves for its own repositories, KG to public portal, Remote-mount a dependency, Build and publish a per-slice SQLite file, A sub-KG is staged in place, then leaves for its own repository, Ask the person, CRDM close-out, CRDM data model, CRDM Phase 6 — implement, MVP, acceptance, CRDM — link the work to an issue, CRDM Phase 1 — needs, CRDM Phases 2–4 — BPA and requirements, CRDM requirements, CRDM Phase 5 — beans and sign-off, Hand back to the discussion, Secure agent permissions, Session state machine, Publish an ArchiMate model — every picture derived from it, A harness’s default rendering, Wireframe design review, Getting started, Authoring a document, Make the content change, Content Change and Review, Content lifecycle, Contributor feedback on a working draft, Draft, review and publish, Editing and HCI validation, Evidence for a recommendation, Make a decided public comment change, Release a draft for public comment, Public comment on a review draft, Record agent step, Review-log watch, Board: open and close content, Board: place a note, Board: relocate content to the trashcan, Classify and code content, DTH authoring, L2 component edit and review, SMART Guideline end to end . A person or an agent arriving at any conformant layer has four verbs available on what they find: . | browse — explore the graph, its subgraphs, its skills, its processes, its schemas and its assets without mutating anything. | materialise — pull a remote harness closure or a subscribed subgraph onto local disk at a pinned commit or recorded digest. | instantiate — scaffold a new folio or harnessed repository from the harness so it can author and publish its own graphs. | copy-into-folio — take a node or asset from a knowledge graph into your own folio (assets[] or folio/), stamp KgAsset.source provenance, and edit, comment or raise todos on your copy. | .

4234.title: The four verbs and their capability floor
4234.content: Three of the four verbs write, and an agent in a read-only container, a viewer on a static site, or a session without repository credentials cannot perform a write. Each verb therefore declares its capability requirement up front and degrades cleanly rather than failing halfway through a procedure. | verb | write capability required | process | governing skills | Tools | read-only degradation | . | browse | none (git-read or published HTTP/files only) | — (stateless read) | kg-navigation, directory-conventions | skill-list, skill-fetch, search-graph, get-neighbors, kg-graph-export | none needed — browse is the read-only floor and must remain completely useful with zero write capabilities | . | materialise | one of git-push, github-api, github-connector (to persist lock/record changes; local worktree write for --staging) | mount-dependency.bpmn, materialize-remote.bpmn | remote-mount, materialize-remote, kg-subscription | remote-mount (mount:remote), mount-from-lock, kg-retrieve-npm | run bun run cat mount:remote --plan or mount:remote:check to inspect the resolved closure and digests without writing | . | instantiate | one of git-push, github-api, github-connector | getting-started.bpmn, repo-conversion.bpmn | folio-init, getting-started, repo-conversion | folio-init (folio_init / bun run cat init-folio) | run folio-init with --dry-run (dry_run: true) to emit the full manifest and file plan as Markdown without touching disk or remote refs | . | copy-into-folio | one of git-push, github-api, github-connector | copy-into-folio.bpmn (for KG assets); copy-out-materialized.bpmn (for materialized library items) | kg-affordances, copy-out-materialized, directory-conventions | declaration-resolution (check:declared-assets), witness-conformance | inspect the upstream asset in place via browse, and emit the target KgAsset declaration snippet (with source pre-filled) so the user can apply it where they have write access | .

4235.title: Why browse requires zero write capability
4235.content: browse is the read-only floor of every conformant knowledge graph: . | On a published site (gh-pages or a CDN), browse reads the exported JSON-LD graph (kg.jsonld), the per-subgraph visualisers, and the rendered BPMN/DMN surfaces over plain HTTP. | In a checkout with an MCP server attached, browse uses skill-list, skill-fetch, search-graph and get-neighbors. | In a bare filesystem checkout with no server and no network, browse reads <name>.json at the layer root, resolves directories[] and assets[], and reads the files directly (kg-navigation). | . No step of browse may require git-push, github-api or github-connector. If a browse tool or visualiser refuses to run because write credentials are absent, that is a defect in the tool.

4236.title: Checking write capability before a writing verb
4236.content: Before starting materialise, instantiate or copy-into-folio, determine which write capability the current environment holds (scenarios/capabilities/): . | git-push — a working tree with push access to the target repository’s remote (git push --dry-run succeeds). | github-api — a GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN or gh auth status capable of creating commits, branches or pull requests via the GitHub API. | github-connector — an MCP GitHub connector (push_files, create_or_update_file, create_pull_request) attached to the session. | . The three states of the capability check are kept distinct: . | Available (git-push, github-api, or github-connector present): proceed with the writing verb using the corresponding tool path. | Absent (probed and none of the three is present): take the read-only degradation branch (--plan, --dry-run, or in-place inspection plus an exportable snippet). Never silently drop the provenance or leave a half-written tree. | Could not determine (the probe itself failed for an environmental reason, such as an unreachable host): report could-not-determine with the probe error; do not report the capability as absent and do not attempt a blind write. | .

4237.title: copy-into-folio and KgAsset.source provenance
4237.content: When a folio owner or authoring agent copies an asset from an upstream knowledge graph into their own folio to adapt it, comment on it or raise todos against it, the process is copy-into-folio.bpmn. Like copy-out-materialized, copying a knowledge-graph asset into a folio is two writes and a refusal: . | Never touch the source graph. The upstream layer is read-only from the copier’s point of view; the arrow runs out of the source lane and never back. | Copy the bytes and declare the asset in the target folio’s <name>.json assets[]. A file copied into an undeclared scratch path is invisible to check:declared-assets and to the folio’s visualisers. | Stamp KgAsset.source (AssetSourceSchema in schemas/kg/kg-node.ts) on the target folio’s KgAsset entry: | . { "id": "adapted-guideline-table", "src": "assets/adapted-guideline-table.json", "role": "guideline-table", "source": { "instance": "litlfred/example-ig", "path": "assets/guideline-table.json", "ref": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567" } } . The three states of KgAsset.source . KgAsset.source ({ instance, path, ref? }) is how the graph tells a copy from original work: . | source state | meaning | . | present, and ref matches upstream | copied from instance at path and current with that upstream commit | . | present, and ref differs or is omitted | copied from instance at path, either adapted locally since ref or taken without a commit pin (staleness is checkable only when ref is recorded) | . | absent (undefined) | authored in this layer — a third state, never “copied from an unknown place” | . A copied asset MUST carry source: without it the copy is indistinguishable from locally authored work, and nothing downstream can reconstruct which layer it came from. Working on the copy in the target folio . Once the asset is declared in the target folio with KgAsset.source stamped and verified by bun run cat check:declaration-resolution (check:declared-assets), it is ordinary writable content of the target folio. The folio owner can edit it in place, attach review comments, or raise todos (todo-manager) against it without disturbing the upstream knowledge graph.

4239.title: Offering the knowledge graph
4239.content: Skill kg-contribution-offer: Ask whether agreed requirements should become knowledge-graph content, and as what — in a form the person can answer by selecting. Use at the end of CRDM sign-off, or whenever a body of agreed work could become a skill, a process, a schema or a work item and nobody has been asked. Offers “none” as a first-class answer. Named by: CRDM Phase 5 — beans and sign-off . When a person is done with requirements on some workflow, ask whether and how to add them to the knowledge graph, and give options. CRDM sign-off is the usual moment: without this step, agreed requirements exist only as an issue and a conversation, and no later agent finds them.

4240.title: What this skill is NOT
4240.content: It is not a decision procedure for where a node goes. That is placement, and it is an agent’s procedure: which layer, which declared graph, which kind of node, which stub convention. Run it after this skill has an answer, not instead of it. It is not general guidance on asking questions. That is interaction-modality §4.1, and this skill does not restate it — it obeys it, and supplies what the options are here. It is not what to do when the author CORRECTS a rule. That is symbiotic-interaction §2, and it runs the other way: the node already exists, the author has just said it is wrong, and the correction is written into it in the same turn without an offer, because offering there asks the author to repeat a correction already made. The line between the two is one question: does the rule already have a home? A ruling on something already in the graph is an edit and needs no offer; a ruling that implies a node which does not exist is this skill’s case, unless the author named the destination themselves. The division in one line: . This skill decides what to offer. symbiotic-interaction §2 decides what needs no offering. placement decides where the answer lands. interaction-modality decides the shape of the asking.

4241.title: The rule
4241.content: The agent never picks a destination silently. An agent that decides on its own that a requirement “is really a skill” and writes one has made a node nobody asked for, in a graph somebody else maintains. If the person does not answer, the default applies — and the default creates nothing.

4242.title: One question, not two
4242.content: “Should this enter the knowledge graph at all” and “as what” are asked as one question: destinations as options, none among them, and a stated default. Two rounds cost a low-dexterity person a real interaction; listing none keeps the single question from forcing an answer.

4243.title: One question for the SET, not one per requirement
4243.content: A CRDM run can agree many requirements. Asking once per requirement is redundant entry (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7), so the offer names the set and asks once. If the person wants different destinations for different items, they say so and the agent asks follow-ups about the ones that differ. That path is opened by their answer, never assumed.

4244.title: The options are DERIVED, never invented
4244.content: The destinations are the graphs this layer declares, in <name>.json — read at the time of asking, never a list typed from memory. Not every declared graph is an authorable destination. A store that is incoming (uploads), derived (qa, health, translation-sources) or a record of something that already happened (issue-marks, memory) is not somewhere a requirement is authored into. Offer the graphs whose nodes a person writes: . | offer | because | . | a skill (cat-harness) | the requirement is a rule an agent must follow | . | a BPMN process (cat-harness) | it is a sequence with lanes and gateways | . | a schema (schemas) | it constrains the shape of data | . | a Tool (tools) | it is a capability with declared io | . | documentation (docs) | it is a design-memory asset — see below | . | a work item (beans) | it is work to be done, not knowledge to be kept | . | an fsh-guts proposal | it is a design not yet agreed — and see the warning below | . | folio content (folio) | it is subject matter, not platform | . | none | it is already captured by the issue and the code | .

4245.title: The design-memory asset, and the question that identifies one
4245.content: A design record — an asset produced while building a feature, accessing data, or managing or rendering a type of content, but not the content to be displayed — goes into docs/. One question separates this class from every other destination: . Was this produced while BUILDING something, rather than being the thing that was built? . A requirement set, an options analysis, a measured comparison, the reasoning behind a schema: each is an artefact of the work rather than its output. It is not subject matter, so it is not folio. It is not a rule an agent follows, so it is not a skill (a skill is read by an agent about to act; a design record by a person asking why is it like this). It is not work outstanding, so it is not a work item. It is memory, and docs/ is where a layer keeps memory a person reads. Not fsh-guts . fsh-guts is the declared non-rendered trashcan, whose content may be thrown away or lost. A proposal not yet agreed can afford to be lost; the reasoning behind something already built cannot. WHOSE docs/ — the owning layer’s, not the repository’s . docs/ is not one place. It is a declared graph, and the layer that owns a harness, feature or tool owns its detailed information, design and planning. Ask placement Step 1’s question: which layer owns this? A design record for a cat-harness feature files in cat-harness/docs/; one for a folio’s own subject matter does not belong in the platform at all. What else belongs there, and the line against a skill . Besides the design record, docs/ holds: . | how to reach the data a piece of content describes — endpoints, credentials policy, shapes, quirks of a source; | everything past the competence line, which is the sharp test: | . A skill carries what a competent practitioner needs IN ORDER TO DO the task. Anything beyond that is documentation. Background, derivations, options not taken, and an API’s full surface when the task touches three calls are documentation. Conversely, a rule an agent must follow, filed in docs/, is a rule skill_fetch will never serve. Where in that layer’s docs/ is placement’s question, not this one. none is a real answer: a requirement whose whole content is “the button should be blue” becomes a commit and nothing else.

4246.title: What the agent does with the answer
4246.content: . | Run placement for the chosen kind — it decides layer, graph and node kind, and catches a hardcoded path or a literal naming one folio. | Create a work item for the authoring work, parented to the feature’s epic. The offer produces a decision, not a node; writing it is work, and work is a work item before it is a file. | Record the answer where the next agent will see it — on the issue, with the round summary issue-working already requires. | . On none, record that too (“asked, answered none, because the requirement is carried by the code”): otherwise it is indistinguishable from never having asked.
